title.zh: 卷五十一 吳書六 宗室傳
title.en: Volume 51: Book of Wu 6 - Biographies of nobles
title.raw: 卷五十一 吳書六 宗室傳 Volume 51: Book of Wu 6 - Biographies of nobles

sentences.zh: 孫靜字幼臺，堅季弟也。

translations.literal: Sun Jing, courtesy name Youtai, was the youngest younger brother of Sun Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jing, styled Youtai, was the youngest of Sun Jian’s brothers.

sentences.zh: 堅始舉事，靜糾合鄉曲及宗室五六百人以為保障，眾咸附焉。

translations.literal: When Sun Jian first raised troops, Jing gathered five or six hundred men from the villages and the clan to serve as a safeguard, and the masses all attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jian first rose in arms, Sun Jing rallied some five or six hundred local men and kinsmen as a protective force, and people flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 策破劉繇，定諸縣。

translations.literal: Ce defeated Liu Yao and pacified the various counties.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce defeated Liu Yao and brought the counties under control.

sentences.zh: 進攻會稽，遣人請靜，靜將家屬與策會於錢唐。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Kuaiji, he sent someone to summon Jing; Jing led his family members and met Ce at Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack on Kuaiji, sent for Sun Jing, and Sun Jing brought his household to join Sun Ce at Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 是時太守王朗拒策於固陵，策數渡水戰，不能克。

translations.literal: At that time the Administrator Wang Lang resisted Ce at Guling; Ce several times crossed the water to give battle but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Wang Lang held Sun Ce off at Guling; Sun Ce tried more than once to force a crossing and fight on the other bank but could not break through.

sentences.zh: 靜說策曰："朗負阻城守，難可卒拔。

translations.literal: Jing urged Ce, saying, “Lang relies on natural obstacles and defends the city; he is hard to take in a hurry.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jing urged Sun Ce: “Wang Lang is dug in behind natural barriers; you cannot expect to storm him overnight.

sentences.zh: 查瀆南去此數十里，

translations.literal: Zha Creek is several tens of li south of here,
translations.idiomatic: Zha Creek lies a few dozen li to the south,

sentences.zh: 〈查音祖加反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Note on pronunciation: the character for Zha is read zu-jia [fanqie].〉
translations.idiomatic: The marginal gloss indicates that Zha takes its initial from zu and its rime from jia.

sentences.zh: 而道之要徑也，宜從彼據其內，所謂攻其無備、出其不意者也。

translations.literal: and it is a crucial path; you ought to advance by that route and seize what lies within—what is called striking where they are unprepared and catching them unawares.
translations.idiomatic: That route is the vital approach; thrust inland along it and strike where they do not expect you.

sentences.zh: 吾當自帥眾為軍前隊，破之必矣。

translations.literal: I shall personally lead the host as the vanguard of the army; we will surely break them.
translations.idiomatic: I will lead the main body myself as the first wave—we will crack them for certain.

sentences.zh: "策曰："善。

translations.literal: ” Ce said, “Good.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun Ce replied, “Good.”

sentences.zh: "乃詐令軍中曰："頃連雨水濁，兵飲之多腹痛，令促具罌缶數百口澄水。

translations.literal: ” Then he falsely announced to the army: “The rains have lately turned the water muddy; the soldiers drinking it have mostly gotten stomachaches—order them quickly to prepare several hundred jars and pots to settle the water.
translations.idiomatic: ” Then he put out a false order: “The river has been silty from all this rain; men who drink it are doubled up with cramps—have them ready hundreds of jars at once to draw off clear water.

sentences.zh: "至昏暮，羅以然火誑朗，便分軍夜投查瀆道，襲高遷屯。

translations.literal: ” At dusk he spread fires to deceive Lang, then divided the army and by night sent them along the Zha Creek road to raid the Gaoxian camp.
translations.idiomatic: ” At nightfall he lit decoy fires to fool Wang Lang, split his force, and marched up the Zha Creek track after dark to strike the camp at Gaoxian.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：今永兴县有高迁桥。〉

translations.literal: 〈Pei Songzhi’s investigation: today in Yongxing County there is a Gaoxian Bridge.〉
translations.idiomatic: (Pei Songzhi notes that Gaoxian Bridge still stands in present-day Yongxing County.)

sentences.zh: 朗大驚。

translations.literal: Lang was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 遣故丹楊太守周昕等帥兵前戰。

translations.literal: He sent the former Danyang Administrator Zhou Xin and others to lead troops forward into battle.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched the former Danyang prefect Zhou Xin and others to take the lead with their men.

sentences.zh: 策破昕等，斬之，遂定會稽。

translations.literal: Ce defeated Xin and the others, beheaded them, and thereupon pacified Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce routed them, killed Zhou Xin, and settled Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：昕字大明。

translations.literal: 〈The Kuaiji Canon Record states: Xin’s courtesy name was Daming.
translations.idiomatic: (According to the Kuaiji dianlu, Zhou Xin’s courtesy name was Daming.

sentences.zh: 少游京师，师事太傅陈蕃，博览群书，明於风角，善推灾异。

translations.literal: In his youth he traveled to the capital and studied under Grand Tutor Chen Fan; he read widely and was skilled in “wind-angle” divination and interpreting anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: He had studied in the capital under Grand Tutor Chen Fan, read widely, and was adept at astrological signs and reading portents.

sentences.zh: 辟太尉府，举高第，稍迁丹杨太守。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the Grand Commandant’s office, ranked at the top of his cohort, and was gradually promoted to Danyang Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Grand Commandant’s service, graduated with highest honors, and rose step by step to prefect of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 曹公起义兵，昕前后遣兵万餘人助公征伐。

translations.literal: When Duke Cao raised the righteous army, Xin in succession sent more than ten thousand troops to assist the duke in his expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao raised his coalition army, Zhou Xin repeatedly sent him upward of ten thousand men for the campaigns.

sentences.zh: 袁术之在淮南也，昕恶其淫虐，绝不与通。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shu was in Huainan, Xin detested his debauchery and cruelty and utterly refused dealings with him.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuan Shu occupied Huainan, Zhou Xin abhorred his cruelty and dissipation and would have nothing to do with him.

sentences.zh: 献帝春秋曰：袁术遣吴景攻昕，未拔，景乃募百姓敢从周昕者死不赦。

translations.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian states: Yuan Shu sent Wu Jing to attack Xin but did not capture him; Jing then promised the common people that whoever dared follow Zhou Xin would be put to death without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiandi Chunqiu records that Yuan Shu sent Wu Jing against Zhou Xin without reducing him; Wu Jing then threatened the populace that anyone who sided with Zhou Xin would die without mercy.

sentences.zh: 昕曰：“我则不德，百姓何罪？

translations.literal: Xin said, “If I lack virtue, what crime have the common people committed?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xin said, “If I am the one at fault, what have the people done wrong?

sentences.zh: ”遂散兵，还本郡。〉

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he dispersed his troops and returned to his native commandery.〉
translations.idiomatic: ” So he sent his soldiers home and withdrew to his own commandery.)

sentences.zh: 表拜靜為奮武校尉，欲授之重任，靜戀墳墓宗族，不樂出仕，求留鎮守。

translations.literal: [Sun Ce] memorialized and appointed Jing Colonel Who Inspires Martial Might, wishing to give him heavy responsibility; Jing was attached to his ancestral graves and clan and did not relish leaving office, and asked to remain to guard and hold the region.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce recommended him as Colonel Who Inspires Martial Might and meant to give him a major post, but Sun Jing was unwilling to leave his family graves and kin and asked instead to stay and hold the territory.

sentences.zh: 策從之。

translations.literal: Ce granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce agreed.

sentences.zh: 權統事，就遷昭義中郎將，終於家。

translations.literal: When Quan assumed direction of affairs, [Jing] was promoted on the spot to General of the Household Gentlemen of Manifest Righteousness and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan took charge, Sun Jing was promoted in place to General of the Household Gentlemen of Manifest Righteousness and ended his days at home.

sentences.zh: 有五子，皓、瑜、皎、奐、謙。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Hao, Yu, Jiao, Huan, and Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons—Hao, Yu, Jiao, Huan, and Qian.

sentences.zh: 皓三子：綽、超、恭。

translations.literal: Hao had three sons: Chuo, Chao, and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao had three sons: Chuo, Chao, and Gong.

sentences.zh: 超為偏將軍。

translations.literal: Chao served as General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chao rose to General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 恭生峻。

translations.literal: Gong fathered Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gong was the father of Sun Jun.

sentences.zh: 綽生綝。

translations.literal: Chuo fathered Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuo was the father of Sun Lin.

sentences.zh: 靜次子瑜

translations.literal: Jing’s second son Yu
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jing’s second son, Sun Yu

sentences.zh: 瑜字仲異，以恭義校尉始領兵眾。

translations.literal: Yu, courtesy name Zhongyi, first took command of troops as Colonel of Respectful Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yu, styled Zhongyi, first led troops with the rank of Colonel of Respectful Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 是時賓客諸將多江西人，瑜虛心綏撫，得其歡心。

translations.literal: At that time many of the guests and generals were men from west of the Yangzi; Yu treated them with modest courtesy and soothed them, winning their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his guests and officers then came from Jiangxi; Sun Yu treated them with humility and won them over.

sentences.zh: 建安九年，領丹楊太守，為眾所附，至萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jian’an he became Administrator of Danyang; he was attached to by the multitude, exceeding ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian’an 9 he became prefect of Danyang and drew more than ten thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 加綏遠將軍。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He was also named General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 十一年，與周瑜共討麻、保二屯，破之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he joined Zhou Yu in a joint expedition against the Ma and Bao camps and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he campaigned with Zhou Yu against the Ma and Bao strongholds and took both.

sentences.zh: 後從權拒曹公於濡須，權欲交戰，瑜說權持重，權不從，軍果無功。

translations.literal: Later he followed Quan to resist Duke Cao at Ruxu; Quan wished to give battle, but Yu urged Quan to hold steady; Quan did not listen, and the army indeed achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied Sun Quan against Cao Cao at Ruxu; Sun Quan wanted a pitched fight, but Sun Yu urged caution—Sun Quan ignored him, and the operation came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 遷奮威將軍，領郡如故，自溧陽徙屯牛渚。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Displays Might and continued to administer the commandery as before, moving his garrison from Liyang to Niuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Displays Might, kept his prefectural post, and shifted his headquarters from Liyang to Niuzhu.

sentences.zh: 瑜以永安人饒助為襄安長，無錫人顏連為居巢長，使招納廬江二郡，各得降附。

translations.literal: Yu appointed Rao Zhu of Yong’an as magistrate of Xiang’an and Yan Lian of Wuxi as magistrate of Juchao, and had them recruit and absorb the two commanderies of Lujiang; each secured submissions and attachments.
translations.idiomatic: He named Rao Zhu of Yong’an magistrate of Xiang’an and Yan Lian of Wuxi magistrate of Juchao and tasked them with drawing in the two Lujiang commanderies—both succeeded in winning surrenders.

sentences.zh: 濟陰人馬普篤學好古，瑜厚禮之，使二府將吏子弟數百人就受業，遂立學官，臨饗講肄。

translations.literal: Ma Pu of Jiyin was devoted to learning and fond of antiquity; Yu treated him generously and had several hundred sons of officers and clerks from the two administrations go to study under him; thereupon he established school officials and personally lectured and instructed.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Pu of Jiyin was a serious scholar of the classics; Sun Yu honored him, sent hundreds of young men from both administrations to study with him, set up school officers, and himself presided over lectures.

sentences.zh: 是時諸將皆以軍務為事，而瑜好樂墳典，雖在戎旅，誦聲不絕。

translations.literal: At that time the generals all devoted themselves to military affairs, whereas Yu delighted in the classics and documents; though amid arms and campaigns, the sound of recitation never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: While other commanders lived only for campaigning, Sun Yu loved books—even in the field he never stopped hearing lessons read aloud.

sentences.zh: 年三十九，建安二十年卒。

translations.literal: At age thirty-nine he died in the twentieth year of Jian’an.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-nine in Jian’an 20.

sentences.zh: 瑜五子：彌、熙、耀、曼、紘。

translations.literal: Yu had five sons: Mi, Xi, Yao, Man, and Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yu left five sons: Mi, Xi, Yao, Man, and Hong.

sentences.zh: 曼至將軍，封侯。

translations.literal: Man rose to general and was enfeoffed as a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Man reached general’s rank and received a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 孫皎字叔朗，始拜護軍校尉，領眾二千餘人。

translations.literal: Sun Jiao, courtesy name Shulang, was first appointed Colonel of the Household Who Guards the Army and commanded a force of over two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiao, styled Shulang, began as Colonel of the Household Who Guards the Army with more than two thousand men under him.

sentences.zh: 是時曹公數出濡須，皎每赴拒，號為精銳。

translations.literal: At that time Duke Cao repeatedly sortied to Ruxu; Jiao went to resist him each time and was reckoned crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Cao Cao probed Ruxu, Sun Jiao went to meet him and earned a reputation as an elite commander.

sentences.zh: 遷都護征虜將軍，代程普督夏口。

translations.literal: He was promoted Chief of Staff and General Who Conquers Captives, replacing Cheng Pu as inspector of Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief of staff and General Who Conquers Captives, succeeding Cheng Pu at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 黃蓋及兄瑜卒，又並其軍。

translations.literal: When Huang Gai and his elder brother Yu died, he also merged their armies.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Gai and his elder brother Sun Yu died, he absorbed their commands as well.

sentences.zh: 賜沙羨、雲杜、南新市、竟陵為奉邑。

translations.literal: He was granted Shaxian, Yundu, Nanxinshi, and Jingling as fief income.
translations.idiomatic: He received the income of Shaxian, Yundu, Nanxinshi, and Jingling as his sustenance fiefs.

sentences.zh: 自置長吏。

translations.literal: He appointed his own magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: He chose his own county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 輕財能施，善於交結，與諸葛瑾至厚。

translations.literal: He was light with wealth and able to give; he was skilled at forming ties and was extremely close to Zhuge Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Open-handed and generous, he excelled at friendships and was especially close to Zhuge Jin.

sentences.zh: 委廬江劉靖以得失，江夏李允以眾事，廣陵吳碩、河南張梁以軍旅，而傾心親待，莫不自盡。

translations.literal: He entrusted Liu Jing of Lujiang with gains and losses, Li Yun of Jiangxia with general affairs, Wu Shuo of Guangling and Zhang Liang of Henan with military matters, and treated them with wholehearted intimacy—none failed to give their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He relied on Liu Jing of Lujiang for counsel on policy, Li Yun of Jiangxia for administration, Wu Shuo of Guangling and Zhang Liang of Henan for military affairs, treated them as intimates, and each repaid him with full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 皎嘗遣兵候獲魏邊將吏美女以進皎，皎更其衣服送還之，下令曰："今所誅者曹氏，其百姓何罪?自今以往，不得擊其老弱。

translations.literal: Jiao once sent troops on patrol who captured border officers’ wives and daughters of Wei to present to Jiao; Jiao changed their clothing and sent them back, issuing an order: “What we now punish is the Cao clan—what crime have the common people? From this time forward, you may not strike their old and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Patrols once brought him captive women from the Wei frontier; Sun Jiao reclothed them and sent them home, declaring: “Our quarrel is with the house of Cao—ordinary people are blameless. From now on do not harm their elderly or children.

sentences.zh: "由是江淮間多歸附者。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon many between the Yangzi and Huai came over to him.
translations.idiomatic: ” People between the Yangzi and the Huai therefore flocked to his banner.

sentences.zh: 嘗以小故與甘寧忿爭，或以諫寧，寧曰："臣子一例，征虜雖公子，何可專行侮人邪!吾值明主，但當輸效力命，以報所天，誠不能隨俗屈典矣。

translations.literal: He once quarreled in anger with Gan Ning over a small matter; someone used this to remonstrate with Ning, and Ning said, “Minister and lord are of one pattern—though the General Who Conquers Captives is the heir’s son, how can he arbitrarily insult others? I have encountered an enlightened ruler; I need only devote my strength and life to repay Heaven—I truly cannot bend to vulgar convention.
translations.idiomatic: He once quarreled with Gan Ning over a trifle; when others urged Gan Ning to yield, Gan Ning replied: “Subject and lord follow the same rule—Sun Jiao may be a lord’s son, but that does not give him leave to bully people. I serve a worthy master; I owe him my life and strength—I will not truckle to mere habit.

sentences.zh: "權聞之，以書讓皎曰：

translations.literal: ” When Quan heard of it, he wrote a letter reproaching Jiao:
translations.idiomatic: ” When Sun Quan heard of it, he wrote Sun Jiao a sharp reproof:

sentences.zh: 自吾與北方為敵，中間十年，初時相持年小，今者且三十矣。

translations.literal: Since I and the north have been enemies, ten years lie between; at first we faced each other when we were young, but now I am nearly thirty.
translations.idiomatic: We have faced the north as foes for a decade now; when we first stood against each other we were still young—today I am almost thirty.

sentences.zh: 孔子言‘三十而立’，非但謂五經也。

translations.literal: The Master said that at thirty one “stands firm”—he did not mean only the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: The Master said “at thirty one stands firm”—he was not talking only about mastering the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 授卿以精兵，委卿以大任，都護諸將於千里之外，欲使如楚任昭奚恤，揚威於北境。

translations.literal: I gave you crack troops and entrusted you with a great charge, chief inspector of the generals a thousand li away, wishing to make you like Chu employing Zhao Xixu, displaying might on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: I gave you picked troops and posted you far off to oversee every general—like Chu using Zhao Xixu to overawe the northern marches.

sentences.zh: 非徒相使逞私志而已。

translations.literal: It was not merely to let each indulge private whim.
translations.idiomatic: That was not so you could indulge private tempers.

sentences.zh: 近聞卿與甘興霸飲，因酒發作，侵陵其人，其人求屬呂蒙督中。

translations.literal: Recently I heard that you drank with Gan Xingba and, fired by wine, bullied the man; that man asked to be placed under Lü Meng’s command.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I hear you drank with Gan Ning, picked a drunken quarrel, and humiliated him—so he asked to transfer under Lü Meng.

sentences.zh: 此人雖粗豪，有不如人意時，然其較略大丈夫也。

translations.literal: That man, though rough and bold, has moments that fall short of others’ wishes; still, in the round he is a great fellow.
translations.idiomatic: He is rough-spirited and can rub people the wrong way, but taken altogether he is a man in full.

sentences.zh: 吾親之者，非私之也。

translations.literal: That I favor him is not from private partiality.
translations.idiomatic: The regard I show him is not private favoritism.

sentences.zh: 我親愛之，卿疏憎之。

translations.literal: I love and esteem him, while you hold him cheap and loathe him.
translations.idiomatic: I esteem him; you slight and resent him.

sentences.zh: 卿所為每與吾違，其可久乎？

translations.literal: What you do repeatedly runs counter to me—how can this last long?
translations.idiomatic: You keep acting against my wishes—how long can that go on?

sentences.zh: 夫居敬而行簡，可以臨民；

translations.literal: To dwell in reverence and act with simplicity may enable one to rule the people;
translations.idiomatic: Gravity of manner and simplicity of conduct fit one to govern;

sentences.zh: 愛人多容，可以得眾。

translations.literal: to love others and bear with them broadly may win the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: generosity toward others wins the crowd.

sentences.zh: 二者尚不能知，安可董督在遠，禦寇濟難乎？

translations.literal: If you cannot grasp even these two, how can you oversee and direct from afar and repel raiders and relieve distress?
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot manage even these, how can you command from a distance or meet invasion and disaster?

sentences.zh: 卿行長大，特受重任，上有遠方瞻望之視，下有部曲朝夕從事，何可恣意有盛怒邪？

translations.literal: You have grown to adulthood and received weighty responsibility; above you there are distant quarters watching you, below you troops attend you morning and night—how can you indulge sudden fits of rage?
translations.idiomatic: You are grown, with heavy duty: the realm watches from afar, your soldiers attend you day and night—how can you indulge blind rage?

sentences.zh: 人誰無過，貴其能改，宜追前愆，深自咎責。

translations.literal: Who among men is without fault? What matters is the ability to mend; you should pursue past errors and blame yourself deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone errs; what counts is reform. Examine what you have done wrong and reproach yourself honestly.

sentences.zh: 今故煩諸葛子瑜重宣吾意。

translations.literal: Now I therefore trouble Zhuge Ziyu again to declare my meaning.
translations.idiomatic: I am sending Zhuge Jin once more to spell this out for you.

sentences.zh: 臨書摧愴，心悲淚下。

translations.literal: As I write this my heart is crushed with grief; sorrow brings tears.
translations.idiomatic: Writing this breaks my heart—I weep as I set it down.

sentences.zh: 皎得書，上疏陳謝，遂與寧結厚。

translations.literal: When Jiao received the letter he submitted a memorial apologizing, and thereafter he and Ning formed a deep bond.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiao answered with a memorial of apology and afterward he and Gan Ning became firm friends.

sentences.zh: 後呂蒙當襲南郡，權欲令皎與蒙為左右部大督。

translations.literal: Later, when Lü Meng was about to raid Nan Commandery, Quan wished to make Jiao and Meng joint supreme commanders of the left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Lü Meng prepared to strike Nan commandery, Sun Quan meant to name Sun Jiao and Lü Meng co–supreme commanders of left and right.

sentences.zh: 蒙說權曰："若至尊以征虜能，宜用之。

translations.literal: Meng said to Quan, “If Your Majesty considers the General Who Conquers Captives capable, you ought to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng told Sun Quan: “If you trust the General Who Conquers Captives, give him sole command.

sentences.zh: 以蒙能，宜用蒙。

translations.literal: If you consider Meng capable, you ought to employ Meng.
translations.idiomatic: If you trust me, give it to me.

sentences.zh: 昔周瑜、程普為左右部督，共攻匯陵，雖事決於瑜，普自恃久將，且俱是督，遂共不睦，幾敗國事，此目前之戒也。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu were joint left and right commanders in the attack on Jiangling; though decisions rested with Yu, Pu relied on being a veteran commander and that both were commanders, so they were mutually ill-disposed and nearly ruined the state’s affairs—this is the warning before our eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu jointly commanded the Jiangling campaign, Zhou Yu made the calls, yet Cheng Pu counted himself the senior officer and co-equal commander—they quarreled and nearly wrecked the enterprise. That lesson is still before us.

sentences.zh: "權寤，謝蒙曰："以卿為大督，命皎為後繼。

translations.literal: ” Quan awoke [to the point], apologized to Meng, and said, “I make you supreme commander and order Jiao to follow as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun Quan saw the point, apologized to Lü Meng, and said: “You shall be supreme commander; Sun Jiao will follow as reserve.

sentences.zh: "禽關羽，定荊州，皖有力焉。

translations.literal: ” In capturing Guan Yu and securing Jing Province, Jiao had a share in the effort.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun Jiao played his part in taking Guan Yu and securing Jing province.

sentences.zh: 建安二十四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-fourth year of Jian’an.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jian’an 24.

sentences.zh: 權追錄其功，封子胤為丹楊侯。

translations.literal: Quan posthumously recorded his merit and enfeoffed his son Yin as Marquis of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan honored his service posthumously and enfeoffed his son Sun Yin as marquis of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 胤卒，無子。

translations.literal: When Yin died he had no son.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yin died without an heir.

sentences.zh: 弟晞嗣。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Sun Xi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 領兵，有罪自殺，國除。

translations.literal: He commanded troops, committed a crime, and killed himself; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops, broke the law, and committed suicide; the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 弟咨、彌。

translations.literal: Younger brothers Zi and Mi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers were Sun Zi and Sun Mi.

sentences.zh: 儀皆將軍，封侯。

translations.literal: Zi and Mi were both generals and were enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Both became generals and received marquisates.

sentences.zh: 咨羽林督，儀無難督。

translations.literal: Zi was Colonel of the Feathered Forest; Mi was Colonel Who Has No Difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zi rose to colonel of the Feathered Forest guard; Sun Mi to colonel Who Has No Difficulty.

sentences.zh: 咨為滕胤所殺，儀為孫峻所害。

translations.literal: Zi was killed by Teng Yin; Mi was murdered by Sun Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zi was killed by Teng Yin; Sun Mi fell victim to Sun Jun.

sentences.zh: 孫奐字季明。

translations.literal: Sun Huan, courtesy name Jiming.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Huan, styled Jiming.

sentences.zh: 兄皎既卒，代統其眾，以揚武中郎將領江夏太守。

translations.literal: After his elder brother Jiao had died, he took command of his forces as General of the Household Gentlemen Who Displays Might and as Administrator of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Sun Jiao died, he inherited the army as General of the Household Gentlemen Who Displays Might and prefect of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 在事一年，遵皎舊跡，禮劉靖、李允、吳碩、張梁及江夏閭舉等，並納其善。

translations.literal: In office one year, he followed Jiao’s old tracks, treating Liu Jing, Li Yun, Wu Shuo, Zhang Liang, and Lü Ju of Jiangxia with courtesy, and adopting their good counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he continued Sun Jiao’s arrangements, honoring Liu Jing, Li Yun, Wu Shuo, Zhang Liang, and Lü Ju of Jiangxia and heeding their sound advice.

sentences.zh: 奐訥於造次而敏於當宮，軍民稱之。

translations.literal: Huan was halting in hasty moments but keen when holding office; soldiers and civilians praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Slow to decide in a pinch but sharp once in harness, he won praise from troops and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 黃武五年，權攻石陽，奐以地主，使所部將軍鮮于丹帥五千人先斷淮道。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huangwu, Quan attacked Shiyang; as local lord Huan had his subordinate General Xianyu Dan lead five thousand men first to cut the Huai road.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangwu 5 Sun Quan attacked Shiyang; as local commander Sun Huan sent General Xianyu Dan with five thousand men to sever the Huai route first.

sentences.zh: 自帥吳碩、張梁五千人為軍前鋒，降高城，得三將。

translations.literal: He personally led Wu Shuo and Zhang Liang with five thousand men as the army’s van, reduced Gaocheng, and captured three generals.
translations.idiomatic: He himself led Wu Shuo and Zhang Liang with another five thousand as the van, took Gaocheng, and seized three enemy generals.

sentences.zh: 大軍引還，權詔使在前住，駕過其軍，見奐軍陳整齊，權歎曰："初吾憂其遲鈍，今治軍，諸將少能及者，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: When the great army withdrew, Quan ordered him to go ahead and stay; his carriage passed that army, and seeing Huan’s troops drawn up in good order, Quan sighed and said, “At first I worried he was slow and dull; now in managing the army few generals can match him—I have no worries.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force pulled back, Sun Quan told him to ride ahead and wait; passing his unit, he saw Sun Huan’s ranks perfectly dressed and said with a sigh: “I used to fear he was sluggish—yet few commanders drill troops like this. I need worry no longer.

sentences.zh: "拜揚威將軍，封沙羨侯。

translations.literal: ” He appointed him General Who Displays Might and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shaxian.
translations.idiomatic: ” He named him General Who Displays Might and marquis of Shaxian.

sentences.zh: 吳碩、張梁皆裨將軍，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Wu Shuo and Zhang Liang were both generals of the band and were granted noble rank as secondary marquises within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shuo and Zhang Liang were both subordinate generals and received noble rank as secondary marquises within the passes.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：初权在武昌，欲还都建业，而虑水道溯流二千里，一旦有警，不相赴及，以此怀疑。

translations.literal: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan states: At first Quan was at Wuchang and wished to move the capital back to Jianye, but he worried that the water route two thousand li upstream would, should alarm arise at once, fail to allow mutual rescue—on this account he hesitated.〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Jiangbiao zhuan: Sun Quan was at Wuchang and wanted to return the capital to Jianye, yet he feared that a two-thousand-li haul upstream would leave him unable to rush reinforcements if trouble struck—hence his reluctance.)

sentences.zh: 及至夏口，於坞中大会百官议之，诏曰：“诸将吏勿拘位任，其有计者，为国言之。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiakou, he held a great assembly of all officials in the dockyard to deliberate and issued an edict: “Generals and clerks, do not be constrained by rank; whoever has a plan, speak for the state.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiakou he convened the full civil and military staff in the harbor works and proclaimed: “Rank does not matter—if anyone has counsel for the realm, speak up.

sentences.zh: ”诸将或陈宜立栅栅夏口，或言宜重设铁锁者，权皆以为非计。

translations.literal: ” Some generals proposed that palisades should be erected at Xiakou, others that heavy iron chains should be set; Quan considered none of these sound plans.
translations.idiomatic: ” Some advised palisading Xiakou, others heavy chains across the river; Sun Quan rejected every such scheme.

sentences.zh: 时梁为小将，未有知名，乃越席而进曰：“臣闻香饵引泉鱼，重币购勇士，今宜明树赏罚之信，遣将入沔，与敌争利，形势既成，彼不敢干也。

translations.literal: At that time Liang was a minor commander and not yet known; he crossed his mat and stepped forward, saying, “Your servant has heard that fragrant bait lures deep fish and heavy bribes buy brave men—now you should clearly establish the credibility of rewards and punishments, dispatch generals into the Mian River to vie with the enemy for advantage; once the posture is set, they will not dare meddle.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang was still a junior officer without reputation; he rose out of turn and said: “Sweet bait draws fish from the depths; rich gifts hire heroes. Make rewards and penalties unmistakable, send forces up the Han to contest the ground—once the situation firms, the enemy will not dare probe.

sentences.zh: 使武昌有精兵万人，付智略者任将，常使严整。

translations.literal: Station ten thousand picked troops at Wuchang and give command to a man of judgment and strategy, keeping them always in good order.
translations.idiomatic: Keep ten thousand elite men at Wuchang under a capable strategist and hold them in constant readiness.

sentences.zh: 一旦有警，应声相赴。

translations.literal: Should alarm arise at once, they can respond and hurry to one another’s aid.
translations.idiomatic: If danger strikes, they can answer the call and march to help.

sentences.zh: 作甘水城，轻舰数千，诸所宜用，皆使备具。

translations.literal: Build Ganshui City and several thousand light craft; whatever each place needs for use, have it all prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Fortify Ganshui and stock thousands of light warboats; equip every point as required.

sentences.zh: 如此开门延敌，敌自不来矣。

translations.literal: In this way open the gates and invite the enemy—the enemy will of themselves not come.
translations.idiomatic: Then leave the front open as bait—the foe will lose the nerve to attack.

sentences.zh: ”权以梁计为最得，即超增梁位。

translations.literal: ” Quan deemed Liang’s plan the best and immediately promoted Liang’s rank beyond the norm.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun Quan judged Sun Liang’s advice best and jumped him several grades.

sentences.zh: 后稍以功进至沔中督。〉

translations.literal: Later he gradually advanced on merit until inspector of the central Mian.〉
translations.idiomatic: He later rose by merit to command the middle Han.)

sentences.zh: 奐亦愛樂儒生，覆命部曲子弟就業，後仕進朝廷者數十人。

translations.literal: Huan likewise loved and delighted in ru scholars; he repeatedly ordered the sons of his command’s households to take instruction, and afterward several tens of them entered office at court.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Huan also cherished scholars and sent his officers’ sons to school; dozens later served at court.

sentences.zh: 年四十，嘉禾三年卒。

translations.literal: At age forty he died in the third year of Jiahe.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty in Jiahe 3.

sentences.zh: 子承嗣，以昭武中郎將代統兵，領郡。

translations.literal: His son Cheng succeeded; as General of the Household Gentlemen Who Displays Martial Might he replaced him in command of the army and continued to administer the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Cheng inherited the post as General of the Household Gentlemen Who Displays Martial Might, kept the troops, and held the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 赤烏六年卒，無子，封承庶弟壹奉奐後，襲業為將。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Chiwu without sons; the court enfeoffed Cheng’s younger half-brother Yi to continue Huan’s line, inheriting the enterprise as a general.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chiwu 6 without an heir; the throne named Sun Cheng’s younger half-brother Sun Yi to continue Sun Huan’s line and carry on as general.

sentences.zh: 孫峻之誅諸葛恪也，壹與全熙、施績攻恪弟公安督融，融自殺。

translations.literal: When Sun Jun executed Zhuge Ke, Yi together with Quan Xi and Shi Ji attacked Ke’s younger brother Rong, who was inspector of Gong’an; Rong killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jun slew Zhuge Ke, Sun Yi joined Quan Xi and Shi Ji against Zhuge Rong, Gong’an garrison commander—Zhuge Rong committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 壹從鎮南遷鎮軍，假節督夏口。

translations.literal: Yi moved from South Conqueror to Army Conqueror, was granted the tally of authority, and commanded Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi rose from South Conqueror to Army Conqueror with ceremonial axe and staff and took charge at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 及孫綝誅滕胤、呂據，據、胤皆壹皆之妹夫也，壹弟封又知胤、據謀，自殺。

translations.literal: When Sun Lin executed Teng Yin and Lü Ju, both Ju and Yin were Yi’s brothers-in-law; Yi’s younger brother Feng also knew of Yin and Ju’s plot and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Lin killed Teng Yin and Lü Ju, both men were Sun Yi’s brothers-in-law; his brother Sun Feng, privy to their conspiracy, also took his own life.

sentences.zh: 綝遣朱異潛襲壹。

translations.literal: Lin sent Zhu Yi to raid Yi by stealth.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin secretly ordered Zhu Yi to strike Sun Yi.

sentences.zh: 異至武昌，壹知其攻己，率部曲千餘口過將胤妻奔魏。

translations.literal: When Yi reached Wuchang and learned they meant to attack him, he led more than a thousand dependents of his command across the river with Teng Yin’s wife and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Learning at Wuchang that they were coming for him, Sun Yi took over a thousand followers and Teng Yin’s wife across the river into Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏以壹為車騎將軍、儀同三司，封吳侯，以故主芳貴人邢氏妻子。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Yi General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremonies equal to the Three Offices, enfeoffed him Marquis of Wu, and gave him the former ruler Fang’s Lady Xing as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Wei named him chariots-and-cavalry general with Three Ducal privileges, marquis of Wu, and married him to Lady Xing, a former consort of Emperor Fang.

sentences.zh: 邢美色妒忌，下不堪命，遂共殺壹及邢氏。

translations.literal: Xing was beautiful and jealous; her subordinates could not endure her commands, whereupon they jointly killed Yi and Lady Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xing was lovely but jealous; her household could not bear her tyranny and murdered both her and Sun Yi.

sentences.zh: 壹入魏

translations.literal: Yi’s entry into Wei
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi’s defection to Wei

sentences.zh: （黃初）

translations.literal: (Huangchu)
translations.idiomatic: (Huangchu reign)

sentences.zh: 三年死。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year.

sentences.zh: 孫賁字伯陽；

translations.literal: Sun Ben, courtesy name Boyang;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ben, styled Boyang,

sentences.zh: 父羌字聖

translations.literal: Father Qiang, styled Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sun Qiang (styled Sheng).

translations.literal: (Yi)
translations.idiomatic: (variant Yi)

sentences.zh: ，堅同產兄也，賁早失二親，弟輔嬰孩，賁自贍育，友愛甚篤。

translations.literal: , was the elder brother born of the same parents as Jian; Ben lost both parents early, while his younger brother Fu was still an infant—Ben fed and raised him himself, and their brotherly affection was deep.
translations.idiomatic: was Sun Jian’s full elder brother. Sun Ben orphaned young while Sun Fu was still in swaddling clothes; Sun Ben raised him, and their bond ran deep.

sentences.zh: 為郡督郵守長。

translations.literal: He served as county postal inspector and magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He worked as county postal inspector and chief.

sentences.zh: 堅於長沙舉義兵，賁去吏從征伐。

translations.literal: When Jian raised the righteous army at Changsha, Ben left office and followed in the campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jian rose at Changsha, Sun Ben resigned his post and joined the war.

sentences.zh: 堅薨，賁攝帥餘眾，扶送靈柩。

translations.literal: When Jian died, Ben assumed command of the remaining host and escorted the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Jian’s death Sun Ben took the surviving troops and bore the bier.

sentences.zh: 後袁術徙壽春，賁又依之。

translations.literal: Later Yuan Shu moved to Shouchun, and Ben again attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan Shu shifted to Shouchun and Sun Ben followed him again.

sentences.zh: 術從兄紹用會稽周昂為九江太守，紹與術不協，術遣賁攻破昂於陰陵。

translations.literal: Shu’s cousin Shao employed Zhou Ang of Kuaiji as Administrator of Jiujiang; Shao and Shu were not harmonious, and Shu sent Ben to defeat Ang at Yinling.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao had appointed Zhou Ang of Kuaiji prefect of Jiujiang; Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu were at odds, so Yuan Shu sent Sun Ben to crush Zhou Ang at Yinling.

sentences.zh: 術表賁領豫州刺史，轉丹楊都尉，行征虜將軍，討平山越。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized Ben as acting Inspector of Yu Province, transferred him to Commandant of Danyang, acting General Who Conquers Captives, and had him pacify the mountain Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu recommended him acting inspector of Yu, moved him to Danyang commandant with acting rank as General Who Conquers Captives, and tasked him with subduing the hill tribes.

sentences.zh: 為楊州刺史劉繇所迫逐，因將士眾還住歷陽。

translations.literal: He was harried by Inspector of Yang Province Liu Yao and therefore led his officers and troops back to garrison Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Harried by Yang inspector Liu Yao, he withdrew his command to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 頃之，術復使賁與吳景共擊樊能、張英等，未能拔。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Shu again sent Ben with Wu Jing jointly to strike Fan Neng, Zhang Ying, and others but could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuan Shu again paired him with Wu Jing against Fan Neng and Zhang Ying without success.

sentences.zh: 及策東渡，助賁、景破英、能等，遂進擊劉繇。

translations.literal: When Ce crossed east, he aided Ben and Jing in defeating Ying, Neng, and the others, then advanced to attack Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce crossed the river he helped Sun Ben and Wu Jing rout Zhang Ying and Fan Neng, then drove on Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 繇走豫章。

translations.literal: Yao fled to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao bolted to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 策遣賁、景還壽春報術，值術僭號，署置百官。

translations.literal: Ce sent Ben and Jing back to Shouchun to report to Shu; it happened that Shu had assumed a royal title and installed the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce sent Sun Ben and Wu Jing to Shouchun to report to Yuan Shu—just as Yuan Shu declared himself king and filled out his court.

sentences.zh: 除賁九江太守。

translations.literal: He appointed Ben Administrator of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He named Sun Ben prefect of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 賁不就，棄妻孥還江南。

translations.literal: Ben did not take office but abandoned wife and children and returned south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ben refused the post, left his family, and went back south of the river.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：袁术以吴景守广陵，策族兄香亦为术所用，作汝南太守，而令贲为将军，领兵在寿春。

translations.literal: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Yuan Shu made Wu Jing defend Guangling; Ce’s cousin Xiang was also employed by Shu as Administrator of Runan, while Ben was made a general leading troops at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: (The Jiangbiao zhuan: Yuan Shu left Wu Jing at Guangling; Sun Ce’s clansman Sun Xiang served Yuan Shu as Runan prefect while Sun Ben held general’s rank at Shouchun.)

sentences.zh: 策与景等书曰：“今征江东，未知二三君意云何耳？

translations.literal: Ce wrote to Jing and the others, saying, “Now we are campaigning east of the Yangzi—I do not know what you gentlemen intend.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce wrote to Wu Jing and company: “We are conquering the east—what do you mean to do.

sentences.zh: ”景即弃守归，贲困而后免，香以道远独不得还。

translations.literal: ” Jing immediately abandoned his post and returned; Ben was hard pressed before he escaped, while Xiang, because the road was distant, alone could not get back.
translations.idiomatic: ” Wu Jing abandoned his command and came over; Sun Ben only slipped away after hardship; Sun Xiang, too far off, could not return.

sentences.zh: 吴书曰：香字文阳。

translations.literal: The Wu shu states: Xiang’s courtesy name was Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu shu gives Sun Xiang’s courtesy name as Wenyang.)

sentences.zh: 父孺，字仲孺，坚再从弟也，仕郡主簿功曹。

translations.literal: His father Ru, courtesy name Zhongru, was Jian’s second cousin once removed and served the commandery as chief clerk and merit assessor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sun Ru, styled Zhongru, was Sun Jian’s second cousin once removed and held county posts as chief clerk and merit officer.

sentences.zh: 香从坚征伐有功，拜郎中。

translations.literal: Xiang followed Jian on campaign with merit and was appointed Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiang campaigned with Sun Jian with distinction and received appointment as gentleman of the palace.

sentences.zh: 后为袁术驱驰，加征南将军，死於寿春。〉

translations.literal: Later he ran errands for Yuan Shu, was additionally appointed General Who Conquers the South, and died at Shouchun.〉
translations.idiomatic: He later served Yuan Shu, added the title General Who Conquers the South, and died at Shouchun.)

sentences.zh: 時策已平吳、會二郡，賁與策征廬江太守劉勳、江夏太守黃祖，軍旋，聞繇病死，過定豫章，上賁領太守，

translations.literal: By then Ce had already pacified the Wu and Kuaiji commanderies; Ben joined Ce in campaigning against Liu Xun, Administrator of Lujiang, and Huang Zu, Administrator of Jiangxia; when the army turned back they heard Yao had died of illness, passed through to settle Yuzhang, and memorialized Ben as acting Administrator,
translations.idiomatic: By then Sun Ce had secured Wu and Kuaiji; Sun Ben joined him against Liu Xun of Lujiang and Huang Zu of Jiangxia. On the march home they learned Liu Yao had died; they swung through Yuzhang to pacify it and Sun Ce petitioned to leave Sun Ben acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：时丹杨僮芝自署庐陵太守，策留贲弟辅领兵住南昌，策谓贲曰：“兄今据豫章，是扼僮芝咽喉而守其门户矣。

translations.literal: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan states: At that time Tong Zhi of Danyang had styled himself Administrator of Luling; Ce left Ben’s younger brother Fu with troops garrisoned at Nanchang and said to Ben, “Elder brother, now holding Yuzhang, you choke Tong Zhi’s throat and guard his gateway.
translations.idiomatic: (The Jiangbiao zhuan: Danyang’s Tong Zhi had seized Luling; Sun Ce posted Sun Ben’s brother Sun Fu at Nanchang and told Sun Ben: “With Yuzhang you grasp Tong Zhi by the throat and bar his door.

sentences.zh: 但当伺其形便，因令国仪杖兵而进，使公瑾为作势援，一举可定也。

translations.literal: You need only watch for a favorable moment, then order Guoyi to advance under arms and have Gongjin make a threatening diversion—a single stroke can settle it.
translations.idiomatic: Wait for your opening, push Sun Guoyi forward under arms, let Zhou Yu feint support—and one blow will finish it.

sentences.zh: ”后贲闻芝病，即如策计。

translations.literal: ” Later Ben heard Zhi was ill and immediately acted on Ce’s plan.
translations.idiomatic: ” When Sun Ben heard Tong Zhi had fallen ill he carried out Sun Ce’s plan at once.

sentences.zh: 周瑜到巴兵，辅遂得进据庐陵。〉

translations.literal: When Zhou Yu reached Baqiu, Fu thereupon succeeded in advancing to occupy Luling.〉
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yu reached Baqiu, Sun Fu pushed forward and seized Luling.)

sentences.zh: 後封都亭侯。

translations.literal: Later he was enfeoffed Marquis of the Metropolitan Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: He was later enfeoffed as marquis of the metropolitan lodge.

sentences.zh: 建安十三年，使者劉隱奉詔拜賁為征虜將軍，領郡如故。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian’an the envoy Liu Yin, bearing an edict, invested Ben as General Who Conquers Captives, continuing to administer the commandery as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian’an 13 imperial envoy Liu Yin arrived with orders naming Sun Ben General Who Conquers Captives while he kept the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在官十一年卒。

translations.literal: He died in office after eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness after eleven years.

sentences.zh: 子鄰嗣。

translations.literal: His son Lin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Lin inherited.

sentences.zh: 鄰年九歲，代領豫章，近封都鄉侯。

translations.literal: At age nine Lin replaced him as leader of Yuzhang and was shortly enfeoffed Marquis of Dou Township.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin took Yuzhang at nine and soon received the marquisate of Dou township.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：邻字公达，雅性精敏，幼有令誉。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: Lin’s courtesy name was Gongda; by nature he was refined, keen, and from youth had a fine reputation.〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu shu: Sun Lin, styled Gongda, was acute and polished and famed even as a boy.)

sentences.zh: 在郡垂二十年，討平叛賊，功績修理。

translations.literal: In the commandery nearly twenty years, he suppressed and pacified rebel bandits; his achievements and administration were orderly.
translations.idiomatic: For almost twenty years in the prefecture he crushed rebels and ran an orderly administration.

sentences.zh: 召還武昌，為繞帳督。

translations.literal: He was summoned back to Wuchang and became commander of the tent guard.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to Wuchang, he commanded the headquarters guard.

sentences.zh: 時太常潘浚掌荊州事，重安長陳留舒燮有罪下獄，浚嘗失燮，欲置之於法。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Ceremonies Pan Jun oversaw Jing Province affairs; the magistrate of Chong’an, Shu Xie of Chenliu, was guilty and imprisoned; Jun had once faulted Xie and wished to apply the law to him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Pan Jun then governed Jingzhou; Shu Xie of Chenliu, magistrate of Chong’an, stood accused—Pan Jun had old grievances and meant to punish him.

sentences.zh: 論者多為有言，浚猶不釋。

translations.literal: Though many debaters spoke on his behalf, Jun still would not release him.
translations.idiomatic: Many pleaded for Shu Xie; Pan Jun still refused to relent.

sentences.zh: 鄰謂浚曰："舒伯膺兄弟爭死，海內義之，以為美談，仲膺又奉國舊意。

translations.literal: Lin said to Jun, “The Shu brothers Boying contended to die for each other—the realm praised their righteousness as a fine tale—and Zhongying moreover embodies the state’s former intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin told Pan Jun: “The Shu brothers once vied to die for honor—the empire admired it—and Zhongying still carries that loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今君殺其子弟，若天下一統，青蓋北巡，中州士人必問仲膺繼嗣，答者雲潘承明殺燮，於事何如?"浚意即解，燮用得濟。

translations.literal: Now if you kill his sons and nephews, should the realm unite and the imperial canopy tour north, gentlemen of the Central Plains will surely ask who succeeds Zhongying—if the answer is ‘Pan Chengming killed Xie,’ how will that stand?” Jun’s intent immediately loosened, and Xie obtained deliverance.
translations.idiomatic: If you execute his kin and the empire is someday reunited, the north will ask after Zhongying’s heir—and answering ‘Pan Jun killed Shu Xie’ will shame you.” Pan Jun relented and Shu Xie was spared.

sentences.zh: 〈《博物志》曰：仲膺名邵。

translations.literal: 〈The Bowuzhi states: Zhongying’s given name was Shao.
translations.idiomatic: (Bowuzhi: Zhongying’s personal name was Shao.

sentences.zh: 初，伯膺亲友为人所杀，仲膺为报怨。

translations.literal: At first Boying’s relatives were murdered by someone; Zhongying avenged the grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Boying’s kin had been murdered; Zhongying took revenge.

sentences.zh: 事觉，兄弟争死，皆得免。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered the brothers vied to die; both were spared.
translations.idiomatic: When discovered they argued over who should die; both were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 袁术时，邵为阜陵长。

translations.literal: During Yuan Shu’s time Shao was magistrate of Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuan Shu, Shao was magistrate of Fuling.

sentences.zh: 亦见江表传。〉

translations.literal: It is also seen in the Jiangbiao zhuan.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan records the same.)

sentences.zh: 鄰遷夏口沔中督、威遠將軍，所居任職。

translations.literal: Lin was promoted inspector of Xiakou and the central Mian and General Who Deters the Distance, carrying out his duties where stationed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin rose to middle-Han–Xiakou inspector and General Who Deters the Distance, performing solid service.

sentences.zh: 赤烏十二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the twelfth year of Chiwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chiwu 12.

sentences.zh: 子苗嗣。

translations.literal: His son Miao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Miao inherited.

sentences.zh: 苗弟旅及叔父安、熙、績，皆歷列位。

translations.literal: Miao’s younger brother Lü and uncles An, Xi, and Ji all held successive offices.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Miao’s brother Sun Lü and uncles Sun An, Sun Xi, and Sun Ji all served in turn.

sentences.zh: 〈吴历曰：邻又有子曰述，为武昌督，平荆州事。

translations.literal: 〈The Wu li states: Lin also had a son named Shu, who was inspector of Wuchang and handled Jing Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu li notes another son, Shu, who commanded Wuchang and Jingzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 震，无难督。

translations.literal: Zhen, Colonel Who Has No Difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhen held the colonelcy Who Has No Difficulty.

sentences.zh: 谐，城门校尉。

translations.literal: Xie, colonel of the Capital Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xie was colonel of the Capital Gates.

sentences.zh: 歆，乐乡督。

translations.literal: Xin, inspector of Lexiang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xin commanded Lexiang.

sentences.zh: 震后御晋军，与张悌俱死。

translations.literal: Later Zhen opposed the Jin army and died together with Zhang Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhen later faced the Jin host and fell beside Zhang Ti.

sentences.zh: 贲曾孙惠，字德施。

translations.literal: Ben’s great-grandson Hui, courtesy name Deshi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ben’s great-grandson Sun Hui, styled Deshi.

sentences.zh: 《惠别传》曰：惠好学有才智，晋永宁元年，赴齐王冏义，以功封晋兴侯，辟大司马贼曹属。

translations.literal: The Separate Biography of Hui states: Hui loved learning and had talent and judgment; in the first year of Yongning of Jin he answered Prince Qi of Qi’s call to righteousness and for merit was enfeoffed Marquis of Jinxing and summoned aide in the bandit bureau of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His appendix: Sun Hui was bookish and clever; in Jin Yongning 1 he joined Prince Sima Jiong’s righteous army, earned the marquisate of Jinxing, and entered the grand marshal’s criminal bureau.

sentences.zh: 冏骄矜僭侈，天下失望。

translations.literal: Jiong was arrogant, presumptuous, and extravagant; the realm lost hope in him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong grew arrogant and wasteful and forfeited the empire’s trust.

sentences.zh: 惠献言於冏，讽以五难、四不可，劝令委让万机，归籓青岱，辞甚深切。

translations.literal: Hui submitted advice to Jiong, using allegories of ‘five difficulties’ and ‘four impossibilities,’ urging him to yield the myriad affairs of state and return to his fief on Qing and Dai—the words were trenchant indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui remonstrated with the ‘five difficulties’ and ‘four impossibilities,’ urging him to surrender power and retire to his Shandong fief—in biting terms.

sentences.zh: 冏不能纳，顷之果败。

translations.literal: Jiong could not accept it; shortly afterward he indeed fell.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong would not listen and soon fell.

sentences.zh: 成都王颖召为大将军参军。

translations.literal: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying summoned him as aide to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying named him grand general’s aide.

sentences.zh: 是时颖将有事於长沙，以陆机为前锋都督。

translations.literal: At that time Ying was about to undertake affairs at Changsha and made Lu Ji advance commander.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying was preparing a Changsha campaign and made Lu Ji vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 惠与机乡里亲厚，忧其致祸，谓之曰：“子盍让都督於王粹乎？

translations.literal: Hui was from the same village as Ji and close to him; fearing disaster for Ji, he said to him, “Why not yield the commander’s post to Wang Cui?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui, Lu Ji’s townsman and friend, feared ruin for him and asked: “Why not give the command to Wang Cui.

sentences.zh: ”机曰：“将谓吾避贼首鼠，更速其害。

translations.literal: ” Ji said, “People would say I shrink from the enemy like a rat—that would hasten my ruin.
translations.idiomatic: ” Lu Ji answered: “They would call me a coward—that would only hasten disaster.

sentences.zh: ”机寻被戮，二弟云、耽亦见杀，惠甚伤恨之。

translations.literal: ” Ji was shortly afterward executed; his two younger brothers Yun and Dan were also killed—Hui deeply grieved for them.
translations.idiomatic: ” Lu Ji was soon executed with his brothers Yun and Dan; Sun Hui mourned bitterly.

sentences.zh: 永兴元年，乘舆幸鄴，司空东海王越治兵下邳，惠以书干越，诡其姓名，自称南岳逸民秦祕之，勉以勤王匡世之略，辞义甚美。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxing the imperial carriage favored Ye; Minister of Works Prince Donghai Sima Yue drilled troops at Xiapi—Hui wrote to Yue under a false name, calling himself the South Mountain recluse Qin Mizhi, urging with handsome phrases the strategy of aiding the king and restoring the age.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxing 1 the court moved toward Ye; Prince Donghai Sima Yue trained troops at Xiapi. Sun Hui wrote under the pseudonym Southern Mountain hermit Qin Mizhi, urging him to rescue the throne.

sentences.zh: 越省其书，榜题道衢，招求其人。

translations.literal: Yue read his letter, posted the title on the roads, and sought the man.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue posted the essay at crossroads and hunted for the author.

sentences.zh: 惠乃出见，越即以为记室参军，专掌文疏，豫参谋议。

translations.literal: Hui then came forward to meet him; Yue immediately made him secretary-aide, solely in charge of documents and participating in counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui revealed himself; Sima Yue made him secretary-aide for drafts and planning.

sentences.zh: 每造书檄，越或驿马催之，应命立成，皆有辞旨。

translations.literal: Whenever he drafted letters or proclamations, Yue sometimes sent relay horses to hurry him; he answered the summons on the spot and finished at once, each piece having polished rhetoric.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yue needed edicts he sometimes sent post riders—Sun Hui composed them on demand, always elegant.

sentences.zh: 累迁显职，后为广武将军、安丰内史。

translations.literal: He rose through prominent posts and later became General Who Displays Might on Campaign and interior minister of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed to high office and ended as campaigning General Who Displays Might and interior minister of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 年四十七卒。

translations.literal: He died at forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 惠文翰凡数十首。〉

translations.literal: Hui’s literary compositions number several tens of pieces in all.〉
translations.idiomatic: His writings ran to several dozen pieces.)

sentences.zh: 孫輔字國儀，賁弟也，以揚武校尉佐孫策平三郡。

translations.literal: Sun Fu, courtesy name Guoyi, was Ben’s younger brother; as Colonel Who Displays Martial Might he assisted Sun Ce in pacifying the three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu, styled Guoyi, was Sun Ben’s younger brother; as Colonel Who Displays Martial Might he helped Sun Ce secure three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 策討丹楊七縣，使輔西屯歷陽以拒袁術，並招誘余民，鳩合遺散。

translations.literal: When Ce campaigned against the seven counties of Danyang he made Fu garrison Liyang to the west to resist Yuan Shu and simultaneously recruit the remaining people and gather scattered fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce struck Danyang’s seven counties he stationed Sun Fu west at Liyang against Yuan Shu while settling refugees.

sentences.zh: 又從策討陵陽，生得祖郎等。

translations.literal: He again followed Ce in campaigning against Lingyang and captured Zu Lang and others alive.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Sun Ce against Lingyang and took Zu Lang prisoner.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：策既平定江东，逐袁胤。

translations.literal: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan states: After Ce had pacified east of the Yangzi he expelled Yuan Yin.
translations.idiomatic: (The Jiangbiao zhuan: once Sun Ce settled the east he drove out Yuan Yin.)

sentences.zh: 袁术深怨策，乃阴遣间使赍印绶与丹杨宗帅陵阳祖郎等，使激动山越，大合众，图共攻策。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu deeply resented Ce and secretly sent covert agents bearing seals and ribbons to Danyang chiefs such as Zu Lang of Lingyang, stirring the mountain Yue to gather a great multitude and jointly plot an attack on Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu bitterly resented Sun Ce and secretly dispatched agents with official seals to Danyang militia leaders like Zu Lang of Lingyang, inciting the hill tribes to mass and strike Sun Ce together.

sentences.zh: 策自率将士讨郎，生获之。

translations.literal: Ce personally led officers and troops to campaign against Lang and captured him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce led his army against Zu Lang in person and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 策谓郎曰：“尔昔袭击孤，斫孤马鞍，今创军立事，除弃宿恨，惟取能用，与天下通耳。

translations.literal: Ce said to Lang, “You once raided me and hacked my saddle; now I raise an army and establish affairs, casting aside old hatred—I only take those who can serve and communicate with the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce told him: “You ambushed me once and hacked my saddle; now that I am founding my command I leave old scores aside—I want men I can use who will answer to the world at large.

sentences.zh: 非但汝，汝莫恐怖。

translations.literal: It is not only you [whom I forgive]; do not be afraid.
translations.idiomatic: That goes for everyone here—you need not fear.

sentences.zh: ”郎叩头谢罪。

translations.literal: ” Lang knocked his head and apologized for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zu Lang kowtowed and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 即破械，赐衣服，署门下贼曹。

translations.literal: Immediately his fetters were broken; he was granted clothing and appointed clerk of the bandit bureau under the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce had his chains struck off, gave him clothes, and named him clerk of the bandit bureau.

sentences.zh: 及军还，郎与太史慈俱在前导军，人以为荣。〉

translations.literal: When the army returned, Lang together with Taishi Ci both served as guides for the van—people considered it glorious.〉
translations.idiomatic: On the march home Zu Lang and Taishi Ci rode as van scouts—a mark of honor.)

sentences.zh: 策西襲廬江太守劉勳，輔隨從，身先士卒，有功。

translations.literal: Ce raided west against Liu Xun, Administrator of Lujiang; Fu accompanied him, himself ahead of officers and men, and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce struck west at Liu Xun of Lujiang, Sun Fu went along, fought in the van, and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 策立輔為廬陵太守，撫定屬城，分置長吏。

translations.literal: Ce established Fu as Administrator of Luling, soothed and settled the dependent cities, and separately appointed magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce named him prefect of Luling, pacified the outlying towns, and placed his own county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 遷平南將軍，假節領交州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Pacifies the South, granted the tally of authority, and appointed Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Pacifies the South with ceremonial axe and staff and took office as inspector of Jiao province.

sentences.zh: 遣使與曹公相聞，事覺，權幽系之。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to communicate with Duke Cao; when the affair came to light, Quan imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He contacted Cao Cao through envoys; when Sun Quan discovered it, he had Sun Fu thrown in chains.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：辅恐权不能保守江东，因权出行东冶，乃遣人赍书呼曹公。

translations.literal: 《Dian lüe》 states: Fu feared Quan could not hold Jiangdong; when Quan traveled to Dongye, he sent someone with a letter to summon Duke Cao.
translations.idiomatic: (The Dian lüe: Sun Fu doubted Sun Quan could hold the south; while Sun Quan was away at Dongye he sent Cao Cao a summons.)

sentences.zh: 行人以告，权乃还，伪若不知，与张昭共见辅，权谓辅曰：“兄厌乐邪，何为呼他人？

translations.literal: The traveler reported it; Quan returned and pretended ignorance; together with Zhang Zhao he saw Fu, and Quan said to Fu, “Elder brother, are you weary and unhappy—why did you call another?
translations.idiomatic: The messenger talked; Sun Quan hurried back and feigned ignorance. With Zhang Zhao he confronted Sun Fu: “Brother, are you so weary of service that you would invite outsiders in?

sentences.zh: ”辅云无是。

translations.literal: ” Fu said there was nothing of the sort.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun Fu denied any such thing.

sentences.zh: 权因投书与昭，昭示辅，辅惭无辞。

translations.literal: Quan thereupon threw the letter to Zhao; Zhao showed it to Fu; Fu was ashamed and had no words.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan tossed the letter to Zhang Zhao, who showed it to Sun Fu—Sun Fu went speechless with shame.

sentences.zh: 乃悉斩辅亲近，分其部曲，徒辅置东。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon he executed all Fu's intimates, divided his command, and relocated Fu eastward.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan then executed Sun Fu’s confidants, split his troops, and banished Sun Fu eastward.)

sentences.zh: 數歲卒。

translations.literal: After several years he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died a few years later.

sentences.zh: 子興、昭、偉、昕，皆歷列位。

translations.literal: His sons Xing, Zhao, Wei, and Xin all held successive offices.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Sun Xing, Sun Zhao, Sun Wei, and Sun Xin all rose through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 孫翊字叔弼，權弟也，驍悍果烈，有兄策風。

translations.literal: Sun Yi, courtesy name Shubi, was Quan's younger brother; fierce, brave, and resolute, he had his elder brother Ce's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi, styled Shubi, was Sun Quan’s younger brother—bold, abrupt, and very like Sun Ce.

sentences.zh: 太守朱治舉孝廉，司空辟。

translations.literal: The Administrator Zhu Zhi nominated him Filially Pious and Incorrupt; the Minister of Works summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhu Zhi nominated him as filially pious and incorrupt; the minister of works called him up.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：翊名俨，性似策。

translations.literal: 《Dian lüe》 states: Yi's given name was Yan; his nature resembled Ce's.
translations.idiomatic: (The Dian lüe gives his personal name as Yan and says his temperament matched Sun Ce’s.)

sentences.zh: 策临卒，张昭等谓策当以兵属俨，而策呼权，佩以印绶。〉

translations.literal: When Ce was near death, Zhang Zhao and others thought Ce should leave the troops to Yan, but Ce called Quan and handed him the seals and ribbons.〉
translations.idiomatic: At Sun Ce’s deathbed Zhang Zhao expected him to pass the army to Sun Yan; Sun Ce instead called Sun Quan and gave him the seals.)

sentences.zh: 建安八年，以偏將軍領丹楊太守，時年二十。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jian'an he became General of the Left and acting Administrator of Danyang; he was twenty years old.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian’an 8 he became general of the left and acting prefect of Danyang at the age of twenty.

sentences.zh: 後卒為左右邊鴻所殺，鴻亦即誅。

translations.literal: Later he was killed by his attendant Bian Hong; Hong was executed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: His bodyguard Bian Hong murdered him and was put to death afterward.

sentences.zh: 〈吴历载翊妻徐节行，宜与妫览等事相次，故列於后孙韶传中。〉

translations.literal: 《Wu li》 records the conduct of Yi's wife Lady Xu—it should follow the affair with Gui Lan and others in order, therefore it is placed later in Sun Shao's biography.〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu li preserves Lady Xu’s story; Pei Songzhi places it with the Gui Lan affair later under Sun Shao.)

sentences.zh: 子松為射聲校尉、都鄉侯。

translations.literal: His son Song was Colonel Who Shoots at Sounds and Marquis of Dou Township.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Song held the colonelcy Who Shoots at Sounds and the marquisate of Dou township.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：松善与人交，轻财好施。

translations.literal: 《Wu lu》 states: Song was good at associating with people, light with wealth and fond of giving.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu lu: Sun Song made friends easily, spent freely, and loved to give.)

sentences.zh: 镇巴丘，数咨陆逊以得失。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Baqiu and repeatedly consulted Lu Xun on gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Stationed at Baqiu, he often asked Lu Xun’s advice on policy.

sentences.zh: 尝有小过，逊面责松，松意色不平，逊观其少释，谓曰：“君过听不以某鄙，数见访及，是以承来意进尽言，便变色，何也？

translations.literal: Once he had a small fault; Xun rebuked Song to his face; Song's expression showed displeasure; Xun watched until he relaxed somewhat and said, “You have overheard me not holding my rustic self cheap and have repeatedly visited me—therefore I answered your intent with full words; why did you change color?
translations.idiomatic: Once Sun Song slipped; Lu Xun scolded him to his face and Sun Song bristled. When he cooled, Lu Xun said: “You honored my humble opinion often enough that I spoke plainly—why turn hostile?

sentences.zh: ”松笑曰：“属亦自忿行事有此，岂有望邪！”〉

translations.literal: ” Song smiled and said, “I too was angry at myself for acting thus—how could I have expected otherwise!”〉
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun Song laughed: “I was furious at myself—I hardly blamed you.”)

sentences.zh: 黃龍三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Huanglong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Huanglong 3.

sentences.zh: 蜀丞相諸葛亮與兄瑾書曰："既受東朝厚遇，依依於子弟。

translations.literal: Shu Chancellor Zhuge Liang wrote to his elder brother Jin: "Having received the eastern court's generous treatment, I cling to the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: Shu’s chancellor Zhuge Liang wrote his brother Zhuge Jin: “The eastern court has treated me generously; I feel bound to its younger men.

sentences.zh: 又子喬良器，為之惻愴。

translations.literal: Moreover Ziqiao is fine timber—I grieve for him.
translations.idiomatic: Your son Ziqiao was gifted—I mourn him keenly.

sentences.zh: 見其所與亮器物，感用流涕。

translations.literal: Seeing the objects he presented to Liang, I was moved to tears when using them.
translations.idiomatic: Each gift your son sent still moves me to tears when I use it.

sentences.zh: "其悼松如此，由亮養子喬咨述故雲。

translations.literal: "He mourned Song thus because Liang's adopted son Qiao informed him—so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: ” That grief targeted Sun Song, or so runs the story Zhuge Qiao passed down.

sentences.zh: 孫匡字季佐，翊弟也。

translations.literal: Sun Kuang, courtesy name Jizuo, was Yi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kuang, styled Jizuo, was Sun Yi’s younger brother.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉茂才，未試用，卒。

translations.literal: Nominated Filially Pious and Incorrupt and Outstanding Talent, before he could be tried in office he died.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated as filially pious and as outstanding talent, he died before taking up a post.

sentences.zh: 時年二十餘。

translations.literal: He was over twenty years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was in his twenties.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：曹休出洞口，吕范率军御之。

translations.literal: 《Jiangbiao zhuan》 states: Cao Xiu emerged at Dongkou; Lü Fan led troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: (The Jiangbiao zhuan: Cao Xiu sortied at Dongkou; Lü Fan opposed him.)

sentences.zh: 时匡为定武中郎将，

translations.literal: At that time Kuang was General of the Household Gentlemen Who Fixes Martial Might,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kuang then held rank as General of the Household Gentlemen Who Fixes Martial Might,

translations.literal: (dispatch)
translations.idiomatic: sent

sentences.zh: 范令放火，烧损茅芒，以乏军用，范即启送匡还吴。

translations.literal: Fan ordered fires set, burning thatch and reeds and exhausting military supplies; Fan immediately memorialized and sent Kuang back to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Fan ordered fires that burned straw stores and crippled the army’s logistics; he memorialized at once and shipped Sun Kuang back to Wu.

sentences.zh: 权别其族为丁氏，禁固终身。

translations.literal: Quan separated his lineage as the Ding clan and confined him for life.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan struck him from the Sun lineage into the Ding clan and imprisoned him for life.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案本传曰：“匡未试用卒，时年二十餘。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates: the main biography states, "Kuang died before trial in office; he was over twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes the main text says Sun Kuang died untested in office in his twenties.

sentences.zh: ”而江表传云吕范在洞口，匡为定武中郎将。

translations.literal: "Yet the Jiangbiao zhuan says Lü Fan was at Dongkou and Kuang was General of the Household Gentlemen Who Fixes Martial Might.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Jiangbiao zhuan places Lü Fan at Dongkou with Sun Kuang already a general.

sentences.zh: 既为定武，非为未试用。

translations.literal: "Since he was Fixing Martial Might, he was not untried.
translations.idiomatic: A general is hardly an untried youth.

sentences.zh: 且孙坚以初平二年卒，洞口之役在黄初三年，坚卒至此合三十一年，匡时若尚在，本传不得云卒时年二十餘也。

translations.literal: "Moreover Sun Jian died in the second year of Chuping; the Dongkou campaign was in the third year of Huangchu—thirty-one years from Jian's death to then; if Kuang were still alive, the main biography could not say he died aged over twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian fell in Chuping 2; Dongkou fell in Huangchu 3—thirty-one years later. Sun Kuang could not still have been “in his twenties.”

sentences.zh: 此盖权别生弟朗，江表传误以为匡也。

translations.literal: "This must be Quan's younger brother born separately, Lang—the Jiangbiao zhuan mistakenly took him for Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: This must be Sun Quan’s younger half-brother Sun Lang—the Jiangbiao zhuan confused him with Sun Kuang.

sentences.zh: 朗之名位见三朝录及虞喜志林也。〉

translations.literal: Lang's name and rank appear in the Records of Three Courts and Yu Xi's Forest of Notes.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lang’s career appears in the San chao lu and Yu Xi’s Zhilin.)

sentences.zh: 子泰，曹氏之甥也，為長水校尉。

translations.literal: His son Tai was the Cao clan's nephew by marriage and served as Colonel of Changan Waters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Tai was a Cao in-law and rose to colonel of Changan waters.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾三年，從權圍新城，中流矢死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiahe he followed Quan in besieging Xincheng and was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiahe 3 he joined Sun Quan’s siege of Xincheng and died to a stray shaft.

sentences.zh: 泰子秀為前將軍、夏口督。

translations.literal: Tai's son Xiu was General of the Van and inspector of Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tai’s son Sun Xiu was General of the Van and commander at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 秀公室至親，握兵在外，皓意不能平。

translations.literal: Xiu was closest kin of the ducal house and held troops abroad—Hao could not stomach it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu was imperial kin commanding troops on the frontier—Sun Hao could not abide it.

sentences.zh: 建衡二年，皓遣何定將五千人至夏口獵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianheng Hao sent He Ding with five thousand men to hunt at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianheng 2 Sun Hao sent He Ding with five thousand men to hunt near Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 先是，民間歛言秀當見圖，而定遠獵，秀遂驚，夜將妻子親兵數百人奔晉。

translations.literal: Before this, folk rumor said Xiu would be plotted against; Ding hunted far away—Xiu was alarmed and by night led wife, children, and several hundred household guards to flee to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors already said Sun Xiu would be framed; when He Ding ranged far afield on “hunt,” Sun Xiu bolted by night with family and hundreds of guards into Jin.

sentences.zh: 晉以秀為驃騎將軍、儀同三司，封會稽公。

translations.literal: Jin appointed Xiu General of Agile Cavalry with ceremonies equal to the Three Offices and enfeoffed him Duke of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Jin named him general of agile cavalry with Three Ducal honors and duke of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：皓大怒，追改秀姓曰厉。

translations.literal: 《Jiangbiao zhuan》 states: Hao was furious and retroactively changed Xiu's surname to Li.
translations.idiomatic: (The Jiangbiao zhuan: Sun Hao was so enraged he renamed Sun Xiu “Li” retroactively.)

sentences.zh: 干宝《晋纪》曰：秀在晋朝，初闻皓降，群臣毕贺，秀称疾不与，南向流涕曰：“昔讨逆弱冠以一校尉创业，今后主举江南而弃之，宗庙山陵，於此为墟。

translations.literal: Gan Bao's 《Jin Ji》 states: When Xiu was at the Jin court, he first heard Hao had surrendered; the ministers all congratulated—Xiu claimed illness and did not attend; facing south he wept and said, "Formerly the Marshal Who Attacks Rebels at twenty founded the realm with a colonel's rank; now the Later Lord raises Jiangnan yet casts it away—the ancestral temples and imperial tombs lie in ruins here.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao’s Jin ji: at the Jin court, when word came that Sun Hao had yielded, ministers rejoiced while Sun Xiu stayed away “ill,” faced south, and wept: “The Marshal Who Attacks Rebels began at twenty with a colonel’s commission; our last lord threw away the south—the ancestral shrines lie in dust.

sentences.zh: 悠悠苍天，此何人哉！

translations.literal: Vast heaven—what manner of men are these!
translations.idiomatic: O vast Heaven—what men have brought us here!

sentences.zh: ”朝廷美之。

translations.literal: The court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court praised him.

sentences.zh: 晋诸公赞曰：吴平，降为伏波将军，开府如故。

translations.literal: 《Jin zhugong zan》 states: When Wu was pacified, he was reduced to General Who Calms the Waves with offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: (The Jin zhugong zan: after Wu fell he was demoted to general who calms the waves but kept his staff.)

sentences.zh: 永宁中卒，追赠骠骑、开府。

translations.literal: He died during Yongning; posthumously honored Agile Cavalry with offices.
translations.idiomatic: He died under Yongning and was posthumously honored as agile cavalry general with full offices.

sentences.zh: 子俭，字仲节，给事中。〉

translations.literal: His son Jian, courtesy name Zhongjie, served as attendant within.〉
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Jian, styled Zhongjie, served as palace attendant.)

sentences.zh: 孫韶字公禮。

translations.literal: Sun Shao, courtesy name Gongli.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shao, styled Gongli.

sentences.zh: 伯父河，字伯海，本姓俞氏，亦吳人也。

translations.literal: His uncle He, courtesy name Bohai, originally surnamed Yu and was also a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Sun He, styled Bohai, born a Yu of Wu.

sentences.zh: 孫策愛之，賜姓為孫，列之屬籍，

translations.literal: Ce loved him, granted him the surname Sun, and enrolled him in the clan register,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce favored him, granted the surname Sun, and entered him on the clan rolls,

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：河，坚族子也，出后姑俞氏，后复姓为孙。

translations.literal: 《Wu shu》 states: He was Jian's nephew by a collateral branch; he went out as heir to his aunt the Yu clan, later restored the surname Sun.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu shu: he was a nephew on Sun Jian’s side, adopted out to the Yu branch, later returned to Sun.)

sentences.zh: 河质性忠直，讷言敏行，有气幹，能服勤。

translations.literal: He was loyal and upright by nature, slow of speech but quick in deed, had courage and capacity, and could endure labor.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and blunt, terse in speech but decisive in action, he had grit and stamina.

sentences.zh: 少从坚征讨，常为前驱，后领左右兵，典知内事，待以腹心之任。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Jian on campaigns, often serving as van leader; later he commanded the left and right troops, managed inner affairs, and was trusted as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: He rode with Sun Jian as van leader, later commanded the household guard and inner offices as a trusted insider.

sentences.zh: 又从策平定吴、会，从权讨李术，术破，拜威寇中郎将，领庐江太守。〉

translations.literal: He again followed Ce in pacifying Wu and Kuaiji, followed Quan against Li Shu; when Shu fell he was appointed General of the Household Gentlemen Who Overcomes Raiders and Administrator of Lujiang.〉
translations.idiomatic: He helped Sun Ce take Wu and Kuaiji, joined Sun Quan against Li Shu, and after Shu’s fall became General of the Household Gentlemen Who Overcomes Raiders and prefect of Lujiang.)

sentences.zh: 後為將軍，屯京城。

translations.literal: Later he became a general and garrisoned Jingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as a general holding Jingcheng.

sentences.zh: 初，孫權殺吳郡太守盛憲，

translations.literal: At first, when Quan killed Wu Administrator Sheng Xian,
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Sun Quan executed Wu prefect Sheng Xian,

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：宪字孝章，器量雅伟，举孝廉，补尚书郎，稍迁吴郡太守，以疾去官。

translations.literal: 《Kuaiji dianlu》 states: Xian's courtesy name was Xiaozhang; his capacity was spacious and grand; nominated Filially Pious and Incorrupt, he filled Gentleman of the Palace Secretary, gradually promoted to Wu Administrator, resigned due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: (The Kuaiji dianlu: Sheng Xian, styled Xiaozhang, was magnanimous; nominated filially pious and incorrupt, he rose from gentleman secretary to Wu prefect, then retired ill.)

sentences.zh: 孙策平定吴、会，诛其英豪，宪素有高名，策深忌之。

translations.literal: When Sun Ce pacified Wu and Kuaiji he executed its heroes; Xian had long had a lofty name and Ce deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce slaughtered Wu’s leading men when he conquered the region; Sheng Xian’s fame made Sun Ce dread him.

sentences.zh: 初，宪与少府孔融善，融忧其不免祸，乃与曹公书曰：“岁月不居，时节如流，五十之年，忽焉已至。

translations.literal: At first Xian was friendly with Junior Mentor Kong Rong; Rong worried he could not escape disaster and wrote to Duke Cao: "Time does not stay; seasons flow like a stream—the fifty years have suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He was Kong Rong’s friend; Kong Rong, fearing for him, wrote Cao Cao: “The years do not linger; seasons rush like water—the fiftieth year is suddenly here.

sentences.zh: 公为始满，融又过二，海内知识，零落殆尽，惟会稽盛孝章尚存。

translations.literal: "You have just reached full fifty; I am past two more—all acquaintances within the seas have scattered and perished; only Kuaiji's Sheng Xiaozhang survives.
translations.idiomatic: You have barely reached fifty; I am two years older—friends across the empire are gone—only Kuaiji’s Sheng Xiaozhang remains.

sentences.zh: 其人困於孙氏，妻孥湮没，单孑独立，孤危愁苦，若使忧能伤人，此子不得复永年矣。
