translations.literal: "That man is trapped by the Sun clan; wife and children are lost; alone he stands solitary and in peril—if worry could injure a man, this youth could not again complete his years.
translations.idiomatic: The Suns hold him captive; his family is ruined; he stands alone in peril—if grief could kill, he would not live out his span.

sentences.zh: 春秋传曰：‘诸侯有相灭亡者，桓公不能救，则桓公耻之。

translations.literal: The Zuo commentary states: 'When feudal lords destroy one another and Duke Huan cannot save them, Duke Huan is shamed.'
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo says: when states destroy each other and Duke Huan cannot rescue them, Duke Huan is disgraced.

sentences.zh: ’今孝章实丈夫之雄也，天下谭士依以扬声，而身不免於幽执，命不期於旦夕，是吾祖不当复论损益之友，而硃穆所以绝交也。

translations.literal: "Now Xiaozhang is truly a champion among men; scholars of the realm rely on him to raise their fame, yet his person cannot escape secret imprisonment—his life may not last from dawn to dusk—then my ancestor ought not again discuss friends of profit and loss, and this is why Zhu Mu severed friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhang is a hero whom scholars invoke for renown, yet he rots in jail—his hours are numbered. My forebears stopped debating friendships of utility for good reason—think of Zhu Mu ending ties.

sentences.zh: 公诚能驰一介之使，加咫尺之书，则孝章可致，友道可弘也。

translations.literal: "If you indeed can gallop a single envoy and add a letter within arm's reach, then Xiaozhang can be brought and the way of friendship enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: Send one courier with a short letter and you can summon him—true friendship needs such gestures.

sentences.zh: 今之少年，喜谤前辈，或能讥平皮柄反。

translations.literal: Today's youth delight in slandering their elders—some mock Xiaozhang (the gloss reads ping with the fanqie pi-bing).
translations.idiomatic: Young men today love traducing their elders—some single out Xiaozhang for ridicule.

sentences.zh: 孝章；

translations.literal: Xiaozhang;
translations.idiomatic: As for Xiaozhang—

sentences.zh: 孝章要为有天下大名，九牧之民所共称叹。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang must possess renown throughout the realm; the people of the Nine Provinces praise him together.
translations.idiomatic: —he bears a name the nine provinces acclaim.

sentences.zh: 燕君市骏马之骨，非欲以骋道里，乃当以招绝足也。

translations.literal: The lord of Yan bought the bones of a swift horse—not to race leagues but to summon steeds beyond compare.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Yan bought dead horses’ bones not for speed but to lure thoroughbreds.

sentences.zh: 惟公匡复汉室，宗社将绝，又能正之，正之之术，实须得贤。

translations.literal: Only you restore the Han house; the ancestral altars verge on extinction yet you can right them—the method of righting them truly requires obtaining the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: You alone can revive the Han as the altars fail—doing so demands worthy men.

sentences.zh: 珠玉无胫而自至者，以人好之也，况贤者之有足乎？

translations.literal: Pearls and jade reach men though they have no legs—because people prize them; how much more men of worth who have legs?
translations.idiomatic: Pearls roll to buyers though legless; worthies walk—will they not come to you?

sentences.zh: 昭王筑台以尊郭隗，隗虽小才，而逢大遇，竟能发明主之至心，故乐毅自魏往，剧辛自赵往，邹衍自齐往。

translations.literal: King Zhao built a terrace to honor Guo Wei; Wei though small talent met great favor and could disclose an enlightened ruler's utmost heart—therefore Yue Yi came from Wei, Ju Xin from Zhao, Zou Yan from Qi.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao raised a terrace for Guo Wei—minor talent, royal favor, and worthies flocked from Wei, Zhao, and Qi.

sentences.zh: 乡使郭隗倒县而王不解，临溺而王不拯，则士亦将高翔远引，莫有北首燕路者矣。

translations.literal: Suppose Guo Wei hung inverted and the king did not release him, faced drowning and the king did not save—then gentlemen would also soar far and none would turn north toward Yan's road.
translations.idiomatic: Had Guo Wei hung upside down without rescue, gentlemen would have flown elsewhere—none would face Yan.

sentences.zh: 凡所称引，自公所知，而有云者，欲公崇笃斯义也，因表不悉。

translations.literal: All I cite you yourself know; I speak thus wishing you to honor this principle deeply—therefore my memorial cannot exhaust it.
translations.idiomatic: You know these precedents; I repeat them only to urge you—and a memorial cannot say it all.

sentences.zh: ”由是徵为骑都尉。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he was summoned as Chief of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: ” The court summoned Sheng Xian as chief of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 制命未至，果为权所害。

translations.literal: The commission had not arrived when he was indeed harmed by Quan.
translations.idiomatic: The orders never reached him—Sun Quan killed him first.

sentences.zh: 子匡奔魏，位至征东司马。〉

translations.literal: His son Kuang fled to Wei and rose to east-conquering marshal.〉
translations.idiomatic: His son fled to Wei and reached east-conquering marshal.)

sentences.zh: 憲故孝廉媯覽、戴員亡匿山中，孫翊為丹楊，皆禮致之。

translations.literal: Xian's former nominees as Filially Pious and Incorrupt Gui Lan and Dai Yuan fled and hid in the mountains; when Sun Yi was Administrator of Danyang, both were courteously brought in.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Xian’s protégés Gui Lan and Dai Yuan hid in the hills until Sun Yi as Danyang prefect coaxed them out.

sentences.zh: 覽為大都督督兵，員為郡丞。

translations.literal: Lan was Grand Commander commanding troops; Yuan was assistant administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Lan became chief commander; Dai Yuan, deputy prefect.

sentences.zh: 及翊遇害，河馳赴宛陵，責怒覽、員，以不能全權，令使奸變得施。

translations.literal: When Yi met murder, He hastened to Waning, rebuked Lan and Yuan for failing to preserve full authority and letting treachery succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Yi died Sun He raced to Wancheng and blamed Gui Lan and Dai Yuan for letting assassins inside.

sentences.zh: 二人議曰："伯海與將軍疏遠，而責我乃耳。

translations.literal: The two deliberated: "Bohai is distant from the general yet singles us out for blame alone.
translations.idiomatic: They whispered: “Sun He barely knows us yet dumps every fault on our heads.

sentences.zh: 討虜若來，吾屬無遺矣。

translations.literal: If the Bandit Smasher comes, we shall leave none alive.
translations.idiomatic: If Sun Quan marches west, we are dead men.

sentences.zh: "遂殺河，使人北迎揚州刺史劉馥，令住歷陽，以丹陽應之。

translations.literal: "Thereupon they killed He, sent men north to welcome Inspector of Yang Province Liu Fu, had him stay at Liyang, and responded with Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: ” They murdered Sun He, welcomed Yang inspector Liu Fu from the north to Liyang, and planned to hand Danyang to Wei.

sentences.zh: 會翊帳下徐元、孫高、傅嬰等殺覽、員。

translations.literal: It happened that Yi's tent followers Xu Yuan, Sun Gao, Fu Ying and others killed Lan and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi’s guards Xu Yuan, Sun Gao, and Fu Ying struck first and killed Gui Lan and Dai Yuan.

sentences.zh: 〈吴历曰：妫览、戴员亲近边洪等，数为翊所困，常欲叛逆，因吴主出征，遂其奸计。

translations.literal: 《Wu li》 states: Gui Lan, Dai Yuan were intimate with Bian Hong and others; repeatedly constrained by Yi, they often wished to rebel; exploiting the Wu ruler's expedition they carried out their treacherous plot.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu li: Gui Lan and Dai Yuan were thick with Bian Hong; Sun Yi hemmed them in until, during the sovereign’s absence, they struck.)

sentences.zh: 时诸县令长并会见翊，翊以妻徐氏颇晓卜，翊入语徐：“吾明日欲为长吏作主人，卿试卜之。

translations.literal: At that time all county magistrates gathered to meet Yi; Yi, because his wife Lady Xu was fairly skilled at divination, went in and spoke to Xu: "Tomorrow I wish to host the chief clerks as master—please try divining it.
translations.idiomatic: Every county magistrate came to call on Sun Yi; knowing Lady Xu could read omens, Sun Yi told her: “Tomorrow I host the senior clerks—cast the stalks for me.

sentences.zh: ”徐言：“卦不能佳，可须异日。

translations.literal: " Xu said, "The hexagram cannot be favorable; you must await another day.
translations.idiomatic: ” She said: “The lines look wrong—we should pick another day.

sentences.zh: ”翊以长吏来久，宜速遣，乃大请宾客。

translations.literal: " Yi thought the chief clerks had waited long and ought quickly to be sent off; thereupon he greatly invited guests.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun Yi thought the clerks had waited long enough and threw a large banquet anyway.

sentences.zh: 翊出入常持刀，尔时有酒色，空手送客，洪从后斫翊，郡中扰乱，无救翊者，遂为洪所杀，迸走入山。

translations.literal: Yi constantly carried a sword when going out; at that time he had taken wine and showed drunken color; he saw guests off empty-handed; Hong struck Yi from behind—the commandery fell into chaos with none to rescue Yi—thus Yi was killed by Hong; Hong fled broken into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi usually wore a sword but saw his guests out drunk and unarmed—Bian Hong struck from behind. The prefecture erupted in chaos; no one defended him; Bian Hong fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 徐氏购募追捕，中宿乃得，览、员归罪杀洪。

translations.literal: Lady Xu offered a reward and hunted him down; only by midnight was he taken; Lan and Yuan shifted blame and executed Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu offered a bounty; they ran Bian Hong down before dawn; Gui Lan and Dai Yuan pinned everything on him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 诸将皆知览、员所为，而力不能讨。

translations.literal: The generals all knew what Lan and Yuan had done but lacked strength to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Every officer knew Gui Lan and Dai Yuan were behind it but could not move against them.

sentences.zh: 览入居军府中，悉取翊嫔妾及左右侍御，欲复取徐。

translations.literal: Lan entered and dwelt in the army headquarters, took all of Yi's concubines and attendants left and right, and wished further to take Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Lan moved into headquarters, seized Sun Yi’s concubines and household staff, and meant to take Lady Xu as well.

sentences.zh: 恐逆之见害，乃绐之曰：“乞须晦日设祭除服。

translations.literal: Fearing that resisting would bring harm, she deceived him, saying, "I beg to wait until the last day of the month to set offerings and lay aside mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing refusal would mean her death, she lied: “Let me wait until month’s end to finish the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: ”时月垂竟，览听须祭毕。

translations.literal: " At that time the month was nearly ended; Lan listened and waited until the offerings finished.
translations.idiomatic: ” The month was almost over; Gui Lan agreed to wait until the sacrifice ended.

sentences.zh: 徐潜使所亲信语翊亲近旧将孙高、傅婴等，说：“览已虏略婢妾，今又欲见偪，所以外许之者，欲安其意以免祸耳。

translations.literal: Xu secretly sent trusted persons to speak to Yi's old intimates among the officers Sun Gao and Fu Ying and others, explaining: "Lan has already seized servant girls; now he again wishes to force himself on me—the reason I outwardly consented is to settle his mind and avoid calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu secretly reached Sun Gao and Fu Ying: “Gui Lan has carried off the maids and now wants me—I agreed outwardly only to calm him.

sentences.zh: 欲立微计，原二君哀救。

translations.literal: I wish to establish a subtle plan—I beg you two gentlemen to pity and save me.
translations.idiomatic: I need a hidden strike—I beg you to save me.

sentences.zh: ”高、婴涕泣答言：“受府君恩遇，所以不即死难者，以死无益，欲思惟事计，事计未立，未敢启夫人耳。

translations.literal: " Gao and Ying answered weeping: "We received the prefect's gracious treatment; the reason we did not immediately die in the disaster is that death would have been without benefit—we wished to think through a plan; the plan had not yet been set so we dared not report to the lady.
translations.idiomatic: ” They wept: “We owed your husband—we held back only to devise something useful.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，实夙夜所怀也。

translations.literal: Today's affair is truly what we have harbored day and night.
translations.idiomatic: We have waited nights for this chance.

sentences.zh: ”乃密呼翊时侍养者二十餘人，以徐意语之，共盟誓，合谋。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they secretly summoned over twenty of those who had attended Yi in service; they communicated Xu's intent to them, jointly swore an oath, and combined plots.
translations.idiomatic: ” They quietly rallied twenty of Sun Yi’s old attendants, shared Lady Xu’s plan, and bound themselves by oath.

sentences.zh: 到晦日，设祭，徐氏哭泣尽哀毕，乃除服，薰香沐浴，更於他室，安施帏帐，言笑欢悦，示无戚容。

translations.literal: When the last day came they set offerings; after Lady Xu had wept and exhausted grief she laid aside mourning clothes, burned incense and bathed, moved to another chamber, hung curtains, spoke and laughed with joy, showing no sorrowful countenance.
translations.idiomatic: On the final day of mourning she wailed her fill, shed the hemp, bathed and perfumed herself, moved to an inner room with bright curtains, and laughed as if light-hearted.

sentences.zh: 大小凄怆，怪其如此。

translations.literal: Great and small were grieved and astonished, wondering at her thus.
translations.idiomatic: The household was stunned—her mood seemed obscene.

sentences.zh: 览密觇视，无复疑意。

translations.literal: Lan secretly observed and no longer doubted.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Lan spied and dropped his guard.

sentences.zh: 徐呼高、婴与诸婢罗住户内，使人报览，说已除凶即吉，惟府君敕命。

translations.literal: Xu summoned Gao and Ying with the maids to fill the inner chambers; she sent someone to report to Lan, saying she had removed the inauspicious and reached the auspicious—only await the prefect's command.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu packed the rooms with maids and messaged Gui Lan that mourning was done—she awaited only his word.

sentences.zh: 览盛意入，徐出户拜。

translations.literal: Lan was greatly pleased and entered; Xu came out the door and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Lan swept in; Lady Xu met him at the door and curtsied.

sentences.zh: 览適得一拜，徐便大呼：“二君可起！

translations.literal: Lan had just received one bow when Xu suddenly shouted aloud: "You two gentlemen may rise!
translations.idiomatic: He barely bent when she shouted: “Now, gentlemen!

sentences.zh: ”高、婴俱出，共得杀览，餘人即就外杀员。

translations.literal: " Gao and Ying both emerged and together succeeded in killing Lan; the others immediately went outside and killed Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun Gao and Fu Ying fell upon Gui Lan; the rest cut down Dai Yuan outside.

sentences.zh: 夫人乃还缞绖，奉览、员首以祭翊墓。

translations.literal: The lady thereupon returned to hemp mourning headband and cord, presented Lan's and Yuan's heads to sacrifice at Yi's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu wrapped herself in mourning again and offered their heads on Sun Yi’s grave.

sentences.zh: 举军震骇，以为神异。

translations.literal: The whole army was shaken and thought it miraculous.
translations.idiomatic: The army stood awestruck.

sentences.zh: 吴主续至，悉族诛览、员餘党，擢高、婴为牙门，其餘皆加赐金帛，殊其门户。〉

translations.literal: When the Wu ruler afterward arrived he executed to the last clan all remaining partisans of Lan and Yuan, promoted Gao and Ying to gate officers, and to the rest granted gold and silk in addition, distinguishing their households.〉
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan arrived he extirpated every follower of Gui Lan and Dai Yuan, raised Sun Gao and Fu Ying to gate captains, heaped gold and silk on the rest, and honored their families.)

sentences.zh: 韶年十七，收河餘眾，繕治京城。

translations.literal: At age seventeen Shao gathered He's remaining host, repaired and ordered Jingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen Sun Shao rallied Sun He’s troops and rebuilt Jingcheng.

sentences.zh: 起樓櫓，修器備議禦敵。

translations.literal: He raised towered engines, repaired implements and equipment, and laid plans to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He raised watchtowers, stocked weapons, and prepared a defense.

sentences.zh: 權聞亂，從椒丘還，過定丹楊，引軍歸吳。

translations.literal: When Quan heard of the disturbance he returned from Jiaoqiu, pacified Danyang en route, and led the army back to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the revolt, Sun Quan raced back from Jiaoqiu, secured Danyang on the way, and marched for Wu.

sentences.zh: 夜至京城下營，試攻驚之，兵皆乘城傳檄備警，歡聲動地，頗射外人，權使曉喻乃止。

translations.literal: By night he camped below Jingcheng and probed with a trial attack to startle them—the troops all mounted the walls, passed writs and stood alert; joyous shouts shook the earth; they shot rather freely at those outside; Quan sent word of dawn before they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He camped under Jingcheng by night and feinted an assault—the garrison manned the walls, passed orders, cheered till the ground shook, and peppered the darkness with arrows until Sun Quan explained himself at dawn.

sentences.zh: 明日見韶，甚器之。

translations.literal: The next day he saw Shao and greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning he met Sun Shao and was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 即拜承烈校尉，統河部曲，食曲阿、丹徒二縣，自置長吏，一如河舊。

translations.literal: He immediately appointed him Colonel Who Upholds Fierce Resolve, commanding He's troops, subsisting on Qu’e and Dantu counties, appointing his own magistrates—exactly as He had formerly done.
translations.idiomatic: He named him Colonel Who Upholds Fierce Resolve over Sun He’s old troops, with revenue from Qu’e and Dantu and the same right to pick county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 後為廣陵太守、偏將軍。

translations.literal: Later he became Administrator of Guangling and General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Guangling prefect and General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 權為吳王，遷揚威將軍，封建德侯。

translations.literal: When Quan became King of Wu he promoted him General Who Displays Might and enfeoffed him Marquis of Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan took the Wu kingship Sun Shao became General Who Displays Might and marquis of Jiande.

sentences.zh: 權稱尊號，為鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: When Quan assumed the imperial title he became General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan declared himself emperor Sun Shao was named General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 韶為邊將數十年，善養士卒，得其死力。

translations.literal: Shao was a frontier general several decades; he was good at nurturing soldiers and won their willingness to die.
translations.idiomatic: For decades on the frontier he fed his men well and earned their lives.

sentences.zh: 常以警疆場遠斥候為務，先知動靜而為之備，故鮮有負敗。

translations.literal: He constantly took warning the borderlands and scouting far as his task; knowing enemy movements beforehand he prepared—therefore he rarely suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on alert patrols, learned enemy moves early, and seldom lost.

sentences.zh: 青、徐、汝、沛頗來歸附，淮南濱江屯候皆徹兵遠徙，徐、泗、江、淮之地，不居者各數百里。

translations.literal: Qing, Xu, Ru, and Pei largely came to submit; Huainan riverbank watch posts all withdrew troops and moved far—along Xu, Si, Jiang, and Huai unsettled lands stretched several hundred li each.
translations.idiomatic: People from Qing, Xu, Ru, and Pei drifted south; Wei stripped its Huai River posts—hundreds of li along Xu-Si-Jiang-Huai stood empty.

sentences.zh: 自權西征，還都武昌，韶不進見者十餘年。

translations.literal: From Quan's western expedition and return capital to Wuchang, Shao did not advance to audience for over ten years.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan marched west and fixed his court at Wuchang, Sun Shao stayed away from audience for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 權還建業，乃得朝覲。

translations.literal: When Quan returned to Jianye he was then able to pay court visit.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Sun Quan moved back to Jianye did Sun Shao appear at court.

sentences.zh: 權問青、徐諸屯要害，遠近人馬眾寡，魏將帥姓名，盡具識之，有問鹹對。

translations.literal: Quan asked about the critical points of the various garrisons in Qing and Xu, the distance and numbers of men and horses, and the names of Wei generals—he knew them all completely; whatever was asked he answered.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan quizzed him on Qing-Xu strongpoints, troop counts, distances, Wei commanders—Sun Shao answered every question from memory.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，儀貌都雅。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi tall; his bearing was refined.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi, composed and handsome.

sentences.zh: 權歡悅曰："吾久不見公禮，不圖進益乃爾。

translations.literal: Quan joyfully said: "I have long not seen Gongli—I did not imagine your advance could be thus.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said with delight: “I have missed you so long—I never guessed you had grown this sharp.

sentences.zh: "加領幽州牧、假節。

translations.literal: "He additionally appointed Inspector of You Province and granted the tally of authority.
translations.idiomatic: ” He added him as inspector of You province with ceremonial axe and staff.

sentences.zh: 赤烏四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Chiwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chiwu 4.

sentences.zh: 子越嗣，至右將軍，越兄楷武衛大將軍、臨成侯，代越為京下督。

translations.literal: His son Yue succeeded; he rose to General of the Right; Yue's elder brother Kai was grand marshal of the martial guard and Marquis of Lincheng, replacing Yue as commander below the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Yue inherited and rose to General of the Right; elder brother Sun Kai was grand marshal of the martial guard and marquis of Lincheng, replacing Sun Yue as capital-zone commander.

sentences.zh: 楷弟異至領軍將軍，奕宗正卿，恢武陵太守。

translations.literal: Kai's younger brother Yi rose to General Who Commands the Army; Yi became minister of the imperial clan; Hui was Administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kai's younger brother became commanding general of the household army; a second Sun Yi headed the ministry for the imperial clan; Sun Hui was prefect of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 天璽元年，征楷為宮下鎮驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi Kai was summoned as agile-cavalry general below the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxi 1 Sun Kai was summoned as palace agile-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 初永安賊施但等劫皓弟謙，襲建業，或白楷二端不即赴討者，皓數遣詰楷。

translations.literal: At first the Yong’an bandits Shi Dan and others kidnapped Hao's younger brother Qian and raided Jianye; someone reported Kai wavered and did not immediately march to punish them—Hao repeatedly sent to rebuke Kai.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong’an rebels seized Sun Hao’s brother Sun Qian and struck Jianye, rumor said Sun Kai hesitated—Sun Hao berated him again and again.

sentences.zh: 楷常惶怖，而卒被召，遂將妻子親兵數百人歸晉，晉以為車騎將軍，封丹楊侯。

translations.literal: Kai was constantly fearful; when he was finally summoned he therefore led wife, children, and several hundred household guards to return to Jin—Jin appointed him General of Chariots and Cavalry and enfeoffed him Marquis of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Living in dread, Sun Kai bolted to Jin with family and hundreds of guards when summoned; Jin named him chariots-and-cavalry general and marquis of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 〈晋诸公赞曰：吴平，降为渡辽将军，永安元年卒。

translations.literal: 《Jin zhugong zan》 states: When Wu was pacified he was reduced to General Who Crosses the Liao and died in the first year of Yongan.
translations.idiomatic: (The Jin zhugong zan: after Wu fell he became general who crosses the Liao and died in Yongan 1.)

sentences.zh: 吴录曰：楷处事严整不如孙秀，而人间知名，过也。〉

translations.literal: 《Wu lu》 states: Kai's handling of affairs was less rigorous than Sun Xiu's, yet he was better known among people—this surpassed reason.〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu lu says Sun Kai ran a looser ship than Sun Xiu yet was more famous—odd praise.)

sentences.zh: 孫桓字叔武，河之子也。

translations.literal: Sun Huan, courtesy name Shuwo, was He's son.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Huan, styled Shuwo, was Sun He’s son.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：河有四子。

translations.literal: 《Wu shu》 states: He had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu shu: Sun He had four sons.)

sentences.zh: 长助，曲阿长。

translations.literal: The eldest Zhu, magistrate of Qu’e.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest Sun Zhu, magistrate of Qu’e.

sentences.zh: 次谊，海盐长。

translations.literal: Next Yi, magistrate of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Next Sun Yi, magistrate of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 并早卒。

translations.literal: Both died early.
translations.idiomatic: Both died young.

sentences.zh: 次桓，仪容端正，器怀聪朗，博学强记，能论议应对，权常称为宗室颜渊，擢为武卫都尉。

translations.literal: Next Huan, whose bearing was correct, whose mind was bright, who studied broadly and memorized strongly, could debate and reply—Quan always called him the Zengzi of the imperial clan and promoted him colonel of the martial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Huan was handsome, quick-witted, learned, and eloquent—Sun Quan called him the clan’s Yan Hui and made him colonel of the martial guard.

sentences.zh: 从讨关羽於华容，诱羽餘党，得五千人，牛马器械甚众。〉

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Guan Yu at Huarong, enticed Yu's remaining followers, gained five thousand men, and oxen, horses, and equipment were very numerous.〉
translations.idiomatic: He joined the strike on Guan Yu at Huarong, lured five thousand of his stragglers, and captured huge herds and gear.)

sentences.zh: 年二十五，拜安東中郎將，與陸遜共拒劉備。

translations.literal: At age twenty-five he was appointed General of the Household Gentlemen Who Pacifies the East and together with Lu Xun resisted Liu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-five he was General of the Household Gentlemen Who Pacifies the East beside Lu Xun against Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 備軍眾甚盛，彌山盈谷，桓投力奮命。

translations.literal: Bei's army host was very strong, filling mountains and valleys; Huan devoted his strength and risked his life.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei’s host covered hills and dales; Sun Huan threw everything into the line.

sentences.zh: 與遜戮力，備遂敗走。

translations.literal: Together with Xun he exerted joint effort; Bei thereupon fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He and Lu Xun strained together until Liu Bei broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 桓斬上

translations.literal: Huan cut Shang—
translations.idiomatic: Sun Huan severed the Shanggui—

translations.literal: (variant dou)
translations.idiomatic: ms. dou

translations.literal: (variant kui)
translations.idiomatic: ms. kui

sentences.zh: 道，截其徑要。

translations.literal: —road and intercepted the vital narrows.
translations.idiomatic: —route and seized the defiles.

sentences.zh: 備逾山越險，僅乃得免，忿恚歎曰："吾昔初至京城，桓尚小兒，而今迫孤乃至此也!"桓以功拜建武將軍，封丹徒侯，下督牛港，作橫江塢，會卒。

translations.literal: Bei crossed mountains and passed defiles, barely escaping; angrily sighing he said: "When I first came to Jingcheng, Huan was still a small child—yet now he presses me to this!" Huan for merit was appointed General Who Establishes Martial Might, enfeoffed Marquis of Dantu, directed Niugang below, built Hengjiang rampart, and happened to die.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei scrambled through the hills barely alive and swore: “When I first saw Jingcheng, Sun Huan was a boy—now he corners me like this!” Sun Huan earned General Who Establishes Martial Might, marquis of Dantu, command at Niugang, built the Hengjiang redoubt, then died.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：桓弟俊，字叔英，性度恢弘，才经文武，为定武中郎将，屯戍薄落，赤乌十三年卒。

translations.literal: 《Wu shu》 states: Huan's younger brother Jun, courtesy name Shuying, by nature was spacious in capacity and accomplished in civil and military arts—General Who Fixes Martial Might, garrisoning Boluo; died thirteenth year of Chiwu.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu shu: younger brother Sun Jun, styled Shuying, genial and able in letters and arms—General Who Fixes Martial Might at Boluo—died Chiwu 13.)

sentences.zh: 长子建袭爵，平虏将军。

translations.literal: Eldest son Jian inherited the noble rank—General Who Pacifies Captives.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest Sun Jian inherited as General Who Pacifies Captives.

sentences.zh: 少子慎，镇南将军。

translations.literal: Younger son Shen, General Who Guards the South.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Sun Shen became General Who Guards the South.

sentences.zh: 慎子丞，字显世。

translations.literal: Shen's son Cheng, courtesy name Xianshi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shen’s son Sun Cheng, styled Xianshi.

sentences.zh: 文士传曰：丞好学，有文章，作萤火赋行於世。

translations.literal: 《Wenshi zhuan》 states: Cheng loved learning and had literary skill; he composed the Rhapsody on Fireflies which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wenshi zhuan: Sun Cheng loved books and wrote the Firefly Fu.)

sentences.zh: 为黄门侍郎，与顾荣俱为侍臣。

translations.literal: He was Gentleman of the Yellow Gates and together with Gu Rong both were attending ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was a yellow-gates gentleman alongside Gu Rong.

sentences.zh: 归命世内侍多得罪尤，惟荣、丞独获全。

translations.literal: In the generation that submitted to the decree, many inner attendants incurred blame and penalty—only Rong and Cheng alone achieved preservation.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu yielded, most palace attendants paid with their lives—only Gu Rong and Sun Cheng survived.

sentences.zh: 常使二人记事，丞答顾问，乃下诏曰：“自今已后，用侍郎皆当如今宗室丞、顾荣畴也。

translations.literal: He constantly had the two men keep records; Cheng answered inquiries—thereupon an edict was issued: "From now on, appointed gentlemen of the attending suite should all be like the imperial-clan Cheng and Gu Rong here.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin ruler often consulted them and decreed: “Future gentlemen-attendants must match Sun Cheng and Gu Rong.

sentences.zh: ”吴平赴洛，为范阳涿令，甚有称绩。

translations.literal: "When Wu was pacified he went to Luoyang and became magistrate of Zhuo in Fanyang—he had very praised achievements.
translations.idiomatic: ” After the conquest he served as magistrate of Zhuo in Fanyang with a fine record.

sentences.zh: 永安中，陆机为成都王大都督，请丞为司马，与机俱被害。〉

translations.literal: During Yongan Lu Ji was grand marshal to Prince Chengdu and invited Cheng as marshal—together with Ji he met murder.〉
translations.idiomatic: In Yongan Lu Ji made him staff officer on Prince Chengdu’s campaign—they died together.)

translations.literal: 【Commentary rubric】
translations.idiomatic: Commentary

sentences.zh: 評曰：夫親親恩義，古今之常。

translations.literal: Commentary states: Intimate kinship and gracious duty are constant from ancient to present.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: kinship and obligation bind all ages.

sentences.zh: 宗子維城，詩人所稱。

translations.literal: Imperial sons are bulwarks of the realm—the poets praise them.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen are the dynastic walls the Odes celebrate.

sentences.zh: 況此諸孫，或贊興初基，或鎮據邊陲，克堪厥任，不忝其榮者乎!故詳著雲。

translations.literal: How much more these grandsons—some aided the founding enterprise, some guarded the frontiers, able to bear their charge and not disgrace their glory! Therefore they are set forth in detail.
translations.idiomatic: These Suns aided the rise or held the marches and lived up to both—so their lives are told at length.
